articles.title: Caiado defende fim do sigilo nos inquéritos do STF em meio a crise | G1
articles.standfirst: O candidato cumpre agenda no Rio Grande do Sul neste sábado (5). Programação do ex-governador de Goiás inclui visita à Expointer, em Esteio.
articles.summary: O candidato  cumpre agenda no Rio Grande do Sul neste sábado (5). Programação do ex-governador de Goiás inclui visita à Expointer, em Esteio.
articles.body:
Ronaldo Caiado, candidato à presidência da República pelo PSD, durante visita à Expointer, em Esteio (RS) — Foto: Reprodução/RBS TV

O candidato do PSD à Presidência da República, Ronaldo Caiado , voltou ao Rio Grande do Sul neste sábado (5). O ex-governador de Goiás visitou a Expointer , feira agropecuária que ocorre no Parque Assis Brasil , em Esteio , na Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre.

"Sou criador de cavalo crioulo, apaixonado pela Expointer. É algo que realmente me motiva, ver a garra, a determinação e a coragem desse povo. Eu quero poder chegar à presidência para poder retribuir o que o gaúcho fez pelo Brasil, resgatando a sua história no centro-oeste e no norte desse país", disse, ao chegar no evento.

Ao citar as investigações referentes a Daniel Vorcaro e o Banco Master, o candidato defendeu que "o Supremo quebre o sigilo de todos os escândalos que existem":

"É inaceitável, e seria um golpe à democracia brasiliera, o povo brasileiro não saber o que consta ali, porque a população sabendo, logicamente não vai votar neste que está comprometido", afirmou.

Caiado também voltou a falar sobre o resultado das pesquisas, que mostram Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL):

"Não é possível nós termos no Brasil dois polos, um contra o outro, as maiores rejeições. Sem dúvida, eles não têm nada pra oferecer ao país. Ao contrário, eles têm a esoconder os escândalos em que eles estão envolvidos, e acho que não é esse o sentimento da população", afirmou.

Na agenda do ex-governador de Goiás, está previsto ainda um almoço com representantes da Federação da Agricultura do RS (Farsul) e visita a outros setores da Expointer.

Em julho deste ano, Caiado já havia visitado o Rio Grande do Sul, quando passou por Santo Ângelo e Porto Alegre.

Na visita, o candidato prometeu alterar a Constituição Brasileira para dar mais autonomia aos estados do país , elevou o tom das críticas ao governo Lula ao comentar a crise comercial com os Estados Unidos e afirmou que "quem está prejudicando a campanha do Flávio (Bolsonaro) é ele mesmo" , quando comentou as relações do candidato do PL com Daniel Vorcaro.

Ao comentar a política externa, Caiado afirmou que Lula estaria estimulando o confronto com Donald Trump por interesse eleitoral, para adotar um discurso de defesa da soberania nacional.

articles.title: Passaporte gigante: sanduíche de 1,2m viraliza em Maceió | G1
articles.standfirst: Lanche inspirado no sanduíche tradicional de Alagoas fez lanchonete de casal ganhar 50 mil seguidores e alavancou vendas.
articles.summary: Lanchonete em Maceió cria passaporte de 1,2 metro. Sanduíche gigante atrai clientes de outros estados e faz negócio familiar bombar nas redes sociais.
articles.body:
Tradicional em Alagoas e conhecido pelo recheio generoso, o passaporte ganhou uma versão que chama atenção antes mesmo da primeira mordida: 1,2 metro de comprimento . O lanche gigante é preparado em uma lanchonete no bairro Eustáquio Gomes, em Maceió , e se tornou uma das principais atrações do negócio nas redes sociais. (Assista acima)

O comerciante Lucas Paulo Nascimento e a esposa, Sílvia Letícia Soares, lançaram a versão gigante em setembro de 2025. A ideia surgiu após o casal ver lanches enormes na internet e decidir adaptar o formato ao sanduíche alagoano.

“Eu disse: se tem um tamanho G, por que não um monstruoso? Queria lançar algo que fosse grande, atrativo e também agradasse ao gosto do nosso cliente”, contou Lucas.

A aposta chamou atenção. Um dos vídeos publicados pela lanchonete ultrapassou 1,1 milhão de visualizações , enquanto o perfil do estabelecimento, que tinha cerca de 10 mil seguidores, passou da marca de 51 mil.

Segundo Lucas, a repercussão também teve reflexos no caixa. O comerciante estima que o faturamento da lanchonete cresceu cerca de 20% após a popularização dos lanches gigantes. A divulgação também passou a atrair clientes de outros estados e até de Portugal.

Passaporte de 1,2 metro vira atração em lanchonete de Maceió. — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

O passaporte é um sanduíche típico de Alagoas, semelhante a um cachorro-quente, mas geralmente mais recheado, com ingredientes que podem incluir salsicha, carne moída, tomate, batata palha e molhos.

Não há registro oficial sobre a origem do nome. Uma lenda local diz que turistas criaram o sanduíche para juntar dinheiro da passagem de volta para casa.

A versão, no entanto, faz parte das histórias populares sobre o prato e não tem comprovação documental.

Passaporte de 1,2 metro vira atração em lanchonete de Maceió e viraliza nas redes sociais — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Antes dos milhares de seguidores e das visualizações nas redes sociais, a história do casal começou de forma bem mais simples. Lucas e Sílvia chegaram a vender coxinhas de R$ 1 na garagem de casa enquanto tentavam estruturar o próprio negócio.

Lucas conta que passou por diferentes bairros de Maceió e chegou a montar uma lanchonete com equipamentos e móveis emprestados. Depois de algumas mudanças, o casal se estabeleceu na parte alta da capital.

A atual lanchonete funciona onde antes era a casa da família. No início, Sílvia vendia lanches em um carrinho na frente do imóvel, enquanto Lucas mantinha outro emprego.

“A gente trabalhava pela manhã e à noite. Chegava aqui e ficava até meia-noite vendendo. Começou a fluir e eu pedi para sair do trabalho porque não estava dando mais para conciliar”, relembrou Lucas.

O crescimento ganhou força quando o comerciante começou a aparecer nos vídeos produzidos para divulgar os produtos. Com o aumento da procura, o espaço também precisou ser ampliado. Atualmente, a lanchonete conta com 15 funcionários e tem capacidade para receber cerca de 100 clientes.

O passaporte gigante custa cerca de R$ 170 , segundo o comerciante, e foi pensado principalmente para ser dividido por grupos. Lucas calcula que, entre dez pessoas, por exemplo, o valor fica em torno de R$ 17 para cada uma.

Apesar do tamanho fora do comum, a receita mantém a proposta do tradicional passaporte alagoano: um sanduíche bem recheado e preparado para sustentar.

Depois do sucesso, Lucas e Sílvia pretendem ampliar o negócio. Entre os planos estão a abertura de novas unidades e a inclusão de outros produtos em tamanho fora do convencional no cardápio, como pizzas gigantes.

Para Lucas, o crescimento representa também a transformação da própria história da família.

“Hoje, aqui onde era a nossa casa, é a nossa loja. Os vídeos têm dado um resultado que eu nem imaginava que teria”, disse.

articles.title: Primeira mulher quilombola do Brasil a conquistar doutorado em direito | G1
articles.standfirst: Tese — uma análise sobre os processos de regularização fundiária e disputas pela posse do território Kalunga — foi aprovada pela Universidade de Brasília (UnB).
articles.summary: Vercilene Francisco Dias defendeu tese na UnB sobre a regularização fundiária do território Kalunga, tornando-se pioneira acadêmica entre mulheres quilombolas.
articles.body:
A advogada Vercilene Francisco Dias se tornou a primeira mulher quilombola do Brasil a conquistar um doutorado em direito .

Sua tese — uma análise sobre os processos de regularização fundiária e as disputas pela posse do território Kalunga — foi aprovada pela Universidade de Brasília ( UnB ) no dia 11 de agosto.

"Eu queria mostrar para a sociedade que a gente era capaz de conseguir chegar naquele espaço também. Era uma coisa minha, da comunidade, mas também era de superação. Porque durante meu processo de graduação e mestrado, eu vi muitas meninas se inspirarem em mim, saírem da comunidade estudar", diz a advogada.

Vercilene cresceu na região do Vão do Moleque, território Kalunga, a 130 km de Cavalcante (GO). Filha de lavradores semianalfabetos, ela aprendeu a ler para ajudar a própria comunidade, deixou a região para estudar e trabalhou como empregada doméstica para bancar os estudos.

🔎 Quilombola: é um termo usado para identificar aqueles "remanescentes de comunidades dos quilombos". Os quilombos eram espaços de liberdade e resistência criados para abrigar pessoas escravizadas.

Vercilene Francisco Dias se tornou a primeira mulher quilombola do Brasil a conquistar um doutorado em direito. — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

Vercilene conta que, quando aprendeu a ler, ela ganhou a função de ler e escrever cartas e documentos na comunidade em que vivia.

Ela começou então a querer entender sobre as disputas territoriais que ocorriam na região. Para estudar, ela precisou sair de casa e foi morar com padrinhos em Tocantins, em 1995. Depois, com uma família de fazendeiros no interior do estado.

Decidida a cursar direito, ela voltou para Goiás e trabalhou como empregada doméstica para bancar os estudos. Em 2011, Vercilene passou no vestibular para cursar direito na Universidade Federal de Goiás ( UFG ) pelo 'UFG Inclui', programa de ação afirmativa para estudantes quilombolas e indígenas.

Foi justamente dentro da faculdade de direito que questões da infância de Vercilene voltaram a aparecer. Ela estranhava o conceito de propriedade que encontrava nos livros, porque era diferente da relação com a terra que ela conhecia desde criança no território Kalunga. Uma inquietação que, anos depois, ajudaria a definir o rumo da vida acadêmica dela.

Em 2016, Vercilene se formou em direito e, logo em seguida, engatou o mestrado em Direito Agrário, também na UFG.

"Eu queria tratar as questões dos conflitos territoriais e a regularização fundiária do território Kalunga. Depois que eu terminei o Direito Agrário, durante o finalzinho do mestrado, eu passei num processo seletivo para trabalhar em Brasília em uma organização de assessoria jurídica", conta.

Depois de duas tentativas para entrar no doutorado e de anos conciliando trabalho e estudo, Vercilene conseguiu que a banca da UnB aprovasse sua tese.

"Para chegar onde eu cheguei, eu nunca deixei de ser quem eu era: a Vercilene, quilombola, do território Kalunga, de conviver com a minha família, de falar a língua da minha família. Eu jamais vou deixar de ser quem eu sou, de viver a vida que eu vivo na comunidade, com a minha família, porque, na verdade, eu cheguei aqui por causa deles também", afirma.

articles.title: Chuva forte e ventania causam estragos em feira no interior de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Cidades como Cerquilho (SP) e Porto Feliz (SP) tiveram locais afetados pela força do vento; não há registro de vítimas.
articles.summary: A chuva no interior de SP causou danos em feira de Cerquilho e no quartel de Porto Feliz, além de registro de granizo em Itapetininga, sem deixar vítimas.
articles.body:
Um temporal com chuva e ventos fortes provocou estragos em cidades do interior de São Paulo na madrugada deste sábado (5).

Em Cerquilho (SP), a estrutura do Feirão da Confecção, Indústria e Comércio (Fecic), que acontecia no município, ficou danificada. Algumas barracas ficaram destruídas.

Um vídeo registrou o momento em que uma das tendas se levantou com a força da ventania. Veja acima.

Em nota, a Associação Comercial de Cerquilho informou que aproximadamente 10% da área do evento foi afetada e permanece interditada preventivamente. Como o restante da feira não foi afetada pelo vendaval, a organização afirmou que o evento segue normalmente.

A Defesa Civil informou que além dos estragos na Fecic, foram registradas três quedas de árvores no município de Cerquilho. Uma na Rua José Batista Alves de Abreu, outra na Avenida João Pilon e uma árvore de pequeno porte na Avenida Washington Luiz. Apesar das ocorrências, não houve registro de vítimas, tampouco de residências danificadas.

Em Itapetininga (SP), alguns bairros registraram chuva de granizo durante a madrugada. De acordo com a Defesa Civil, choveu 16 milímetros no município. Em Capão Bonito (SP), foram 21 mm.

Chuva forte e ventania danificaram estrutura da Fecic em Cerquilho (SP) — Foto: Adilson Lima / Imagens cedidas

Porto Feliz (SP) também registrou ventos fortes durante a manhã de sábado (5). A sede do Corpo de Bombeiros na cidade sofreu com a ventania que destelhou a garagem da instituição.

De acordo com a prefeitura, o local já estava passando por uma obra no telhado e, por isso, as telhas ficaram soltas e acabaram sendo levadas pelo vento. Segundo a administração não há registro de ocorrências com vítimas na cidade.

O Corpo de Bombeiros emitiu uma nota informando que não houve registro de danos estruturais à edificação ou às viaturas operacionais da unidade. Todos os funcionários evacuaram do local no momento do destelhamento.

articles.title: Robério Paulino faz caminhada no Alecrim | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato ao governo do RN esteve no bairro e distribuiu panfletos, ouviu comerciantes e falou sobre propostas para comércio, habitação e geração de emprego.
articles.summary: Robério Paulino, candidato do Psol ao governo do RN, fez caminhada no Alecrim nesta sexta-feira (5) e defendeu revitalização do Centro Histórico e construção de moradias populares.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo do Rio Grande do Norte pelo Psol, Robério Paulino, realizou uma caminhada com apoiadores pelo bairro do Alecrim, em Natal .

Durante a agenda, o candidato distribuiu panfletos, ouviu pedidos de comerciantes sobre a necessidade de reformas no camelódromo e também de obras de infraestrutura. Robério Paulino conversou com lojistas sobre propostas para a reestruturação do centro comercial da capital e incentivos ao setor industrial.

O candidato também declarou apoio à proposta de emenda à Constituição que estabelece o fim da escala 6 por 1. Em conversa com apoiadores, ele reforçou a necessidade de revitalização do Centro Histórico de Natal com a construção de moradias sociais.

Dentro do projeto de governo, Robério Paulino destacou o plano para a construção de 50 mil moradias em parceria com o governo federal. Segundo ele, a proposta tem como objetivo atender à demanda habitacional, além de estimular a indústria e gerar emprego e renda no estado.

“A Cidade Alta, infelizmente, está virando deserto, está em uma decadência muito grande. Nós queremos revitalizar o comércio da Cidade Alta e também transformar aquela área, quem sabe, numa área de moradia popular. Nosso plano é a construção de 50 mil moradias populares em regime de mutirão para dinamizar a indústria, gerar emprego, gerar riqueza no estado e atender a grande demanda por habitação do nosso estado.”

Os candidatos ao governo do Rio Grande do Norte Rodrigo de Bolsonaro, do Agir, Robério Paulino, do Psol, e Dário, do PSTU, têm direito à exibição de compromissos de campanha a cada 15 dias, como ficou acertado em reunião com as assessorias das candidaturas. Os três pontuaram entre 1% e 4% na pesquisa Quaest divulgada no último dia 24 de agosto.

articles.title: Incêndio atinge pátio de empresa em Ipatinga e destrói caminhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Fogo também atingiu um galpão de 40 metros quadrados no bairro Parque Veneza na madrugada deste sábado (5). Bombeiros utilizaram oito mil litros de água para conter o incêndio.
articles.summary: Fogo também atingiu um galpão de 40 metros quadrados no bairro Parque Veneza na madrugada deste sábado (5). Bombeiros utilizaram oito mil litros de água para conter o incêndio.
articles.body:
Incêndio atingiu pátio de empresa em Ipatinga — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros/Divulgação

Um incêndio atingiu o pátio de uma empresa no bairro Parque Veneza, em Ipatinga , na madrugada deste sábado (5). O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado por volta das 2h e encontrou vários caminhões em chamas e o galpão de aproximadamente 40 metros quadrados tomado pelo fogo.

Segundo os bombeiros, ainda da área externa foi possível visualizar um cavalo mecânico com carreta, um caminhão-caçamba e outro cavalo mecânico já destruídos pelas chamas.

Para ter acesso ao pátio, os militares precisaram pular o portão e, pelo lado de dentro, utilizar uma ferramenta para abri-lo e permitir a entrada do caminhão de combate a incêndio.

Com uma atuação rápida, os bombeiros conseguiram preservar uma carreta, que teve apenas a lanterna e a lateral esquerda danificadas pelas chamas.

Ainda de acordo com os bombeiros, a equipe também concentrou os esforços para evitar que o fogo atingisse duas pás-carregadeiras que estavam próximas ao galpão, que já estava tomado pelo fogo. Com a chegada de outro caminhão de combate a incêndio, de Coronel Fabriciano, foi possível atuar em mais frentes até o controle e a extinção do incêndio.

Chamas foram controladas pelo Corpo de Bombeiros — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros/Divulgação

Um cavalo mecânico também foi danificado pelo fogo na cabine, mas as chamas não se propagaram para outras partes do veículo.

O gerente da empresa esteve no local e foi orientado pelos bombeiros a retirar as máquinas que estavam na área de risco. Ele não soube informar as possíveis causas do incêndio. Foram utilizados cerca de 8 mil litros de água para conter o fogo.

O candidato ao governo do Rio Grande do Norte pelo Agir, Rodrigo de Bolsonaro, esteve na Redinha Nova, em Extremoz, nesta sexta-feira (5). Ele se reuniu com a candidata a vice-governadora, Socorro Batista, moradores, lideranças comunitárias, correligionários e trabalhadores da reciclagem.

articles.title: Envio de jumentos para abate quase triplicou no PI: procura pela pele e desvalorização do animal podem ter impulsionado alta | G1
articles.standfirst: O Piauí enviou cerca de 3,5 mil jumentos para abate em frigoríficos da Bahia entre janeiro e agosto de 2026, segundo a Agência de Defesa Agropecuária do Estado (Adapi).
articles.summary: O Piauí enviou cerca de 3,5 mil jumentos para abate em frigoríficos da Bahia entre janeiro e agosto de 2026, segundo a Agência de Defesa Agropecuária do Estado (Adapi).
articles.body:
Pesquisadores ouvidos pelo g1 avaliam que o crescimento do envio de jumentos do Piauí para abate em frigoríficos da Bahia pode estar relacionado à desvalorização do animal no meio rural e ao aumento da demanda internacional pela pele. Segundo a Adapi, cerca de 3,5 mil animais foram enviados para o estado vizinho entre janeiro e agosto de 2026.

O número é quase três vezes maior que o registrado em todo o ano de 2025. No mercado asiático, cada pele pode ser vendida por até R$ 4 mil.

De acordo com a Adapi, o município de Marcos Parente , no Sul do Piauí, concentra a maior quantidade de asininos destinados ao abate no estado, segundo a Adapi. Eles são comprados por proprietários e reunidos em uma propriedade rural até o momento do embarque.

População do jumentos no Brasil era de 376 mil cabeças em 2017, segundo o IBGE — Foto: Camila Lima/SVM

Além da oferta de animais a baixo custo, o crescimento da demanda internacional também contribui para o aumento dos abates. Segundo Raniel Lustosa, a China reduziu significativamente a população de jumentos nas últimas décadas e passou a buscar a matéria-prima em outros países.

A principal finalidade do abate é a retirada da pele, utilizada na produção do ejiao, produto tradicional da medicina chinesa e que é produzido a partir do colágeno presente na pele do jumento. Nos frigoríficos brasileiros, a pele passa por tratamento e conservação antes de ser exportada para a China.

"Esse é um produto utilizado na medicina chinesa, nem tanto comprovada [cientificamente], mas é utilizado há milhares de anos e que, vamos dizer assim, faz parte da questão cultural deles. Então, é um produto que tem uma importância, tem um nicho de mercado para os consumidores da China", explicou.

A pesquisadora Patrícia Tatemoto ressaltou que a pele é o principal produto de interesse econômico desses abates, mas que a carne também é exportada como subproduto.

"No passado, acreditava-se que era um jumento que tinha pelagem escura, que era o ideal para essa finalidade, de aumentar o capital estético da pessoa, de beleza, mas depois, com a redução das populações de jumentos, eles passaram a consumir todos os jumentos", explicou Patrícia.

Jumentos passaram a ser vendidos por preços baixos

Segundo o professor universitário e doutor em ciência animal Raniel Lustosa, o jumento, historicamente utilizado no transporte e em atividades agrícolas, perdeu espaço com a mecanização do campo. Em muitas regiões, passou a ser considerado um animal sem utilidade econômica.

“Essa baixa utilização, junto com a proliferação desordenada, faz com que eles sejam comercializados por valores muito baixos”, explicou Raniel.

Para a pós-doutoranda no Instituto de Ciências Biomédicas da USP e consultora de campanha no Brasil pela organização britânica The Donkey Sanctuary, Patrícia Tatemoto, essa desvalorização contribuiu para que a atividade com os jumentos assumisse um caráter extrativista.

O período de reprodução também precisa ser considerado. A gestação dura cerca de 12 meses e, após o nascimento, o animal leva aproximadamente 18 meses para atingir uma idade considerada adequada para o abate. Ao todo, são cerca de dois anos e meio entre a reprodução e a chegada do animal ao frigorífico.

“Não existe uma valorização comercial desses animais. O que existe é uma atividade extrativista. Ninguém produz em fazendas esses animais, porque leva anos para ele ficar pronto para abate e gestação é longa, de até um ano. Custa caro. Então, essa atividade só se mantém dessa forma extrativista”, contou.

Cada pele pode ser vendida por até R$ 4 mil

Enquanto o jumento é adquirido por valores entre R$ 50 e R$ 150, o valor da pele aumenta ao longo da cadeia comercial.

Segundo Raniel Lustosa, uma pele pode ser comercializada pelo frigorífico por cerca de R$ 1 mil a R$ 1,5 mil. No mercado oriental, o produto pode alcançar valores entre R$ 2 mil e R$ 4 mil, dependendo do processamento e do tipo de produto final.

“A gente está falando de um animal que é adquirido por valores irrisórios, de R$ 50, R$ 100, R$ 150, e cuja pele pode chegar a valores de R$ 2 mil a R$ 4 mil no mercado oriental”, destacou.

Criação pode levar cerca de dois anos e meio

Para o professor, uma alternativa seria estruturar uma cadeia produtiva organizada, com produtores cadastrados, associações e cooperativas, em vez da retirada aleatória de animais.

Ele defende que frigoríficos e investidores interessados no mercado estabeleçam acordos com produtores para criar os animais de forma controlada e legalizada.

Viagem pode passar de 1,3 mil quilômetros

Os jumentos são transportados em caminhões. A partir de Marcos Parente, principal ponto de origem dos animais, a distância até os frigoríficos da Bahia pode ultrapassar 1,3 mil quilômetros.

O percurso é de cerca de 1.141 quilômetros até Amargosa (BA) e de 1.314 quilômetros até Itapetinga (BA).

Durante o transporte, os responsáveis devem seguir regras de bem-estar animal. Entre as exigências estão respeitar a capacidade dos caminhões e realizar paradas para alimentação e hidratação em viagens com duração superior a 12 horas. Também é proibido usar instrumentos de choque durante o embarque dos animais.

A demanda pela emissão de Guias de Trânsito Animal (GTAs), documento obrigatório para o transporte dos animais, também reflete o cenário. Em 2026, foram emitidas mais de 70 guias. Em 2025, foram 26, e em 2024, apenas oito, ano em que 303 jumentos foram enviados para abate.

Após a emissão da GTA, a Adapi acompanha os animais apenas até a saída do Piauí. O monitoramento ocorre em Cristalândia, no Sul do estado, onde funciona um posto fixo de fiscalização agropecuária.

A conferência da quantidade de jumentos que chega aos frigoríficos é realizada por fiscais federais responsáveis pela inspeção do abate nos estabelecimentos de destino.

Segundo Daniela Rabelo, o compartilhamento de informações entre a Adapi e os órgãos de fiscalização da Bahia ocorre "Somente se solicitado".

articles.title: Maestro Chico Pinheiro, referência da cultura popular maranhense, morre aos 71 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Artista sofreu um infarto em casa neste sábado (5) e deixou um legado ligado ao bumba meu boi, ao carnaval e à formação de músicos.
articles.summary: Artista sofreu um infarto em casa neste sábado (5) e deixou um legado ligado ao bumba meu boi, ao carnaval e à formação de músicos.
articles.body:
O maestro, arranjador e compositor Francisco de Jesus Araújo Pinheiro , conhecido como Chico Pinheiro , morreu aos 71 anos neste sábado (5), em São Luís . Segundo informações preliminares, ele sofreu um infarto em casa.

Chico era um dos principais nomes da música e da cultura popular do Maranhão. Ele dedicou décadas à formação de músicos e a trabalhos ligados ao bumba meu boi, ao carnaval e ao canto coral.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não havia informações sobre o local e o horário do velório.

Chico Pinheiro, referência da música maranhense, morre aos 71 anos — Foto: Reprodução/Companhia Barrica

Segundo nota divulgada pela Secretaria Municipal da Cultura de São Luís (Secult), Chico Pinheiro participou da fundação do Coral São João, em 1977, integrou o Boizinho Barrica e teve atuação importante na Companhia Barrica.

Seus trabalhos incluíram arranjos ligados ao bumba meu boi, ao carnaval, ao canto coral e a outras expressões da cultura popular.

O maestro também comandou o Bloco Bicho Terra, um dos símbolos do carnaval e das festas populares de São Luís . Ele ajudou a levar as toadas e a percussão maranhense para palcos do Brasil e de outros países.

Ainda segundo a Secult, Chico Pinheiro também era advogado e professor de música aposentado do Instituto Federal do Maranhão (IFMA). Ao longo da carreira, ele pesquisou os ritmos e a musicalidade do estado.

De acordo com a Escola de Música do Maranhão, Chico Pinheiro também atuou como instrumentista, regente e pesquisador. A instituição destacou a contribuição do artista para a formação de gerações e para a valorização da cultura maranhense.

articles.title: Acidente em Duartina: Carro em alta velocidade capota na avenida | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente ocorreu neste sábado (05), na Avenida Nove de Julho. Segundo apuração da TV TEM, a equipe do SAMU foi acionada para atender o motorista do carro que capotou. O outro motorista não se feriu.
articles.summary: Acidente em Duartina envolve carro em alta velocidade que capotou na Avenida Nove de Julho; SAMU socorreu o motorista idoso após a colisão.
articles.body:
Veículo capota após colisão com caminhonete em Duartina (SP) — Foto: Marcus Vinicius Anjos/TV TEM

Um carro em alta velocidade colidiu com uma caminhonete em Duartina (SP), neste sábado (5).

Segundo apurado pela TV TEM , o veículo, conduzido por um idoso, trafegava em alta velocidade pela Avenida Nove de Julho quando, ao realizar uma curva, colidiu com uma caminhonete que seguia à sua frente no mesmo sentido da via.

Com a colisão, o idoso perdeu o controle do automóvel e capotou. Equipes do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foram acionadas para socorrê-lo e retirá-lo do veículo.

articles.standfirst: Segundo a ViaMobilidade, homem apresentou sinais de desorientação neste sábado (5) e caiu na via após a chegada de um trem à plataforma, em Barueri. Ele foi socorrido.
articles.summary: Segundo a ViaMobilidade, homem apresentou sinais de desorientação neste sábado (5) em Barueri. Ele foi socorrido.
articles.body:
Um homem passou mal, na manhã deste sábado (5), e caiu no vão entre um trem e a plataforma na estação Jardim Silveira, da Linha 8-Diamante, em Barueri, Grande São Paulo.

Vídeo divulgado e cedido pela página Jandira da Depressão no Instagram mostra o resgate da vítima (veja acima) .

Segundo a ViaMobilidade, concessionária responsável pela operação da linha, o homem apresentou sinais de desorientação e caiu na via logo após a chegada de um trem à plataforma.

Agentes de Atendimento e Segurança (AAS) prestaram socorro imediato ao homem, que foi encaminhado a um hospital para avaliação médica. O estado de saúde dele não foi divulgado.

Em nota, a ViaMobilidade lamentou o incidente e reforçou a importância de os passageiros respeitarem as sinalizações de segurança nas plataformas e durante o embarque.

A concessionária afirmou ainda que realiza campanhas de conscientização, com painéis informativos e avisos sonoros e visuais nas estações.

articles.title: Incêndio destrói quarto de casa no interior do RN | G1
articles.standfirst: Fogo começou em um ventilador, segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros. Moradores controlaram parte das chamas antes da chegada da equipe.
articles.summary: Incêndio destruiu um quarto de uma casa em Baraúna, no RN, neste sábado (5). Fogo teria começado em um ventilador e causou desabamento do teto.
articles.body:
Um incêndio destruiu um quarto de uma residência no bairro Subestação, em Baraúna , interior do Rio Grande do Norte, na manhã deste sábado (5). Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros de Mossoró, as chamas teriam começado em um ventilador que estava no cômodo.

O fogo destruiu roupas, cama e guarda-roupa que estavam no quarto. O calor também provocou o desabamento do teto.

De acordo com os bombeiros, o incêndio foi percebido pelo filho da proprietária da casa, que dormia no quarto. Moradores conseguiram controlar parte das chamas antes da chegada da equipe.

A residência possui placas de energia fotovoltaica, mas, segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, o fogo não atingiu os equipamentos.

Após chegar ao local, a equipe realizou o resfriamento do cômodo e apagou os focos que ainda permaneciam no imóvel. O quarto foi isolado após o atendimento.

Incêndio destruiu quarto de casa em Baraúna — Foto: Cedida

O Corpo de Bombeiros orienta que, em caso de incêndio, a rede elétrica geral seja desligada, desde que seja seguro fazer isso.

Em seguida, as pessoas devem deixar o imóvel e acionar imediatamente o Corpo de Bombeiros pelo 193.

articles.title: Census 2027: The 14 questions and why opposition fears an NPR 'backdoor'
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Although six years late, enumerators have started knocking on doors for the decennial headcount in Ladakh and snowbound regions such as Jam.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Although six years late, enumerators have started knocking on doors for the decennial headcount in Ladakh and snowbound regions such as Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand starting September 1.But doubts and fears have preceded the Census, turning what was meant to be a routine exercise to track population growth and aid policy planning into a fresh political flashpoint.Until now, the caste census had been the main point of contention between the opposition and the government. The opposition had questioned the intent and methodology of an exercise being conducted in the country after almost 100 years.The contention has now moved beyond the caste census, and the opposition is also raising questions over the methodology of population enumeration, alleging that it too has a “deeper nefarious purpose”.What is the controversy?On August 14, the Centre notified the list of questions that officials will ask during population enumeration. The questionnaire, however, contains 14 new or modified questions compared with the 2011 Census.These include spouse's name, nationality as declared, father's particulars, mother's particulars, SC/ST/caste, literacy and digital literacy, highest educational level attained and stream/discipline, place of Covid-19 vaccination, total number of bank accounts, mobile number, Aadhaar number, voter ID number, passport number for Indian passport holders, and availability of a driving licence.Interestingly, several of these questions, including details of a person's father and mother and their places of birth, were also part of the National Population Register (NPR) schedule notified in 2020.Moreover, the Union Budget presented on February 1 this year allocated Rs 6,000 crore for the NPR and Census 2027, even though the government has not yet notified any schedule for the NPR.The Budget document said the allocation included provisions for the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India and various schemes of the Registrar General of India, with Rs 6,000 crore earmarked for NPR and Census 2027.What are the opposition's chargesFollowing the notification of the questionnaire, the opposition has accused the Centre of turning the Census exercise into a “backdoor for the NPR, and eventually, NRC”.Congress Rajya Sabha member Jairam Ramesh said the methodology of asking questions in Census 2027 is flawed and alleged that questions on religion, date of birth, place of birth and parents' details had never been asked in previous enumerations.“Census is confidential. Clearly, Census 27 has a deeper nefarious purpose,” he said in a post on X.Similarly, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee alleged that the Centre was planning to conduct the Census in the form of NPR.“They have started the census. Census in the form of NPR. You have to provide your bank account number, mobile number and Aadhaar number. You must disclose the full details of all family members,” Mamata said.“No political party has been informed. At least the Trinamool Congress was not informed. Nobody knows whose name will be deleted. Is it going to be another SIR? Who knows,” she added.Even during the run-up to the Bengal assembly elections, she alleged that the Centre was planning to 'take away' people's citizenship in the name of NRC.Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan also raised questions over the inclusion of the new questions, arguing that the Census should not be used to divide people.“The reported inclusion of questions about parents’ place of birth and religion in the upcoming Census is deeply troubling. The Census must not become a backdoor for the NPR and, eventually, the NRC. Citizenship cannot be tied to religion, and no census should be used to divide our people. The Union Government must immediately drop such divisive questions. Secular forces must stand united against this dangerous move,” Vijayan said.Difference between Census and NPRCensus and NPR differ in their legal basis, objectives and the nature of information they are designed to collect.The Census is a statistical exercise meant to produce data on population, literacy, occupation, migration, housing and, in 2027, caste. It is used for making policies, allocating resources and delimitation.On the other hand, the National Population Register is a continuously updated register of “usual residents” created under the Citizenship Act, 1955.It is designed to maintain an identifiable database of people who have lived in a locality for at least six months or intend to stay there for the next six months, irrespective of their citizenship.The NPR collects detailed identity information, including names, parents' particulars, place of birth, nationality as declared, address and identity documents such as Aadhaar, voter ID and passport, as well as mobile numbers. The data collected through NPR is linked to the proposed National Register of Citizens.Under Rule 3 of the Citizenship Rules, the Centre may order preparation of the National Population Register, from which the Local Register of citizens is prepared after verification.Rule 4 provides that individuals whose citizenship is doubtful can be flagged in the Population Register for further enquiry.The NPR data was first collected in 2010 alongside the 2011 Census house-listing exercise and updated through a door-to-door survey in 2015.However, both the Census and NPR are conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Union Ministry of Home Affairs.Can Census data be shared?The inclusion of the new questions has raised a larger question: Can information collected during the Census be accessed or used by government agencies for purposes beyond the exercise itself?The law says no. Section 15 of the Census Act, 1948 provides a strong legal shield around personal information collected during the Census.“No person shall have a right to inspect any book, register or record made by a census-officer in the discharge of his duty,” the Act says.“No entry in any such book, register, record or schedule shall be admissible as evidence in any civil proceeding whatsoever or in any criminal proceeding other than a prosecution under this Act or any other law for any act or omission which constitutes an offence under this Act,” it further says.This means that the information collected through the census cannot be used by other government agencies to determine the citizenship of a person.Speaking to The Times of India, advocate Ajinkya Udane said it would therefore be incorrect to accuse the government of divulging information collected through the Census.“Through the census, private information of people is being asked. However, the Census Act bars the government from divulging this information to its agencies,” Udane said.“So, to accuse the government of doing something which the law bars it from doing is not correct,” he added.Cyber and privacy law expert advocate Prashant Mali, however, stressed that Census data must remain a statistical instrument and “not become a backdoor for state surveillance”.“Section 15 of the Census Act creates a strong statutory confidentiality barrier. Individual census records are not open to inspection and are not admissible as evidence. Therefore, census information cannot legitimately be converted into an evidentiary database for citizenship determination merely because another government authority wants to use it,” Mali said.He said that even if a census record, or personal information traceable back to it, is accessed or used in a manner prohibited by Section 15, describing it as “independent intelligence” would not cure the underlying violation.“Substance must prevail over form. If the underlying census record or identifiable information has been accessed or used contrary to Section 15, I feel calling it independent intelligence does not cure the problem,” he said.“I feel the State cannot do indirectly through a citizenship inquiry what Section 15 of the Census Act prohibits it from doing directly through the Census record. A lawful purpose for processing does not automatically create a lawful source of data,” he told The Times of India.During the conversation, Mali said that the interaction between the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) and the Census Act will also be interesting to watch during the exercise.“DPDPA (Digital Personal Data Protection Act) Sections 3–17 are scheduled to come into force 18 months after 13 November 2025, i.e. 13 May 2027, while Census 2027 field operations occur around that period,” Mali said.“This makes the interaction between the Census Act and DPDPA particularly interesting for the 2027 exercise,” he added.The Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) is primary law which will dictate how the personal data is collected, processed and stored.It sets out obligations for entities handling personal data - such as obtaining consent, limiting use to the stated purpose, and ensuring data security - and grants individuals rights over their own data, including access and correction.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: New police team to crackdown on illegal number plates across England
articles.summary: It will bring together forces across England to target organised crime groups and drivers who dodge fines.
articles.body:
A centralised crackdown on illegal number plates will target organised crime groups and drivers who dodge fines by bringing together data and information from police forces across England, the government has said.

The newly-created National Roads Policing Coordination Centre (NRPCC) will see improved collaboration across forces as well as new technology, such as specialist goggles that can detect number plates that have been made unreadable to cameras.

Illegal number plates are often used by organised crime groups to move stolen goods and to evade speeding, parking and clean air zone penalties, the Department for Transport (DfT) said.

Drivers with incorrectly displayed or missing number plates can be fined up to £1,000.

Illegal number plates can come in many forms including cloned plates - which copy the registration of a legitimate vehicle - and ghost plates - where a transparent film is used to make them undetectable to cameras.

Vehicles that hide from number plate recognition cameras are harder for police to track down when they are stolen or linked to crimes.

Policing and crime minister Sarah Jones said: "Illegal number plates are not a victimless offence.

"They are used by criminals to avoid detection, move illegal goods and stay one step ahead of law enforcement."

She said by bringing forces together and making better use of technology the new team would track down offenders faster and disrupt gangs.

Ch Supt Marc Clothier, deputy national co-ordinator for the NRPCC, said: "The police forces involved in our ghost plates operation have shown how effective a targeted and intelligence-led approach is in tackling offenders as well as educating and supporting drivers in ensuring their number plates are compliant."

articles.title: Nepal floods show the risk; China's mega-dam raises bigger questions for India
articles.summary: India News: The rain came down relentlessly, turning quiet mountain streams into raging torrents and narrow roads into muddy rivers. Across Nepal, floodwaters and.
articles.body: The rain came down relentlessly, turning quiet mountain streams into raging torrents and narrow roads into muddy rivers. Across Nepal, floodwaters and debris swept through homes, roads and hydropower facilities, leaving behind broken bridges, stranded communities and villages cut off from the outside world.In the mountains, where steep slopes already make life precarious, swollen rivers, landslides and collapsing rock can quickly turn a natural hazard into a cascading disaster.For communities living along narrow Himalayan valleys, a sudden rush of water, ice and debris can leave little time to escape.The recent flash floods in Nepal have brought these vulnerabilities sharply into focus. Search teams have battled heavy rain and thick layers of debris while looking for people believed to be trapped in tunnels, hydropower projects and underground power facilities along the Bhotekoshi River.But the devastation has also raised a larger question: what happens when the already fragile Himalayan environment is combined with increasingly large infrastructure projects, including dams, tunnels, highways and hydropower facilities?That question has particular significance for India because the Himalayas are not confined by political boundaries. Rivers, glaciers, mountain systems and geological faults cut across China, Nepal, Bhutan and India. A disaster originating in the high mountains can therefore have consequences far beyond the point where it begins.It is against this backdrop that China's massive hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo, known downstream as the Brahmaputra, has come under renewed scrutiny.The project, being built in Tibet's Medog County at the dramatic Great Bend of the river, is expected to become the world's largest hydropower project.Its location, however, adds another layer of concern. The project sits in one of the world’s most geologically challenging regions, marked by steep Himalayan terrain, active faults, earthquakes, landslides, glaciers and extreme weather.These natural risks make the dam not just a massive engineering undertaking, but also a strategically sensitive project located upstream of one of India’s most important rivers.Why the Brahmaputra is so importantChina formally began construction of the Yarlung Tsangpo River Lower Reaches Hydropower Project in July last year. The mega-dam is being built in Medog County, near the river’s Great Bend, where the Yarlung Tsangpo makes a dramatic U-turn before entering India.China calls the Brahmaputra the Yarlung Tsangpo. After crossing into Arunachal Pradesh, the river is known as the Siang or Dihang before flowing through Assam and eventually entering Bangladesh, where it is known as the Jamuna.The project is located in one of the world’s deepest river gorges. Over a stretch of about 50 kilometres, the river drops nearly 2,000 metres, creating enormous potential for hydropower generation.The project is expected to comprise five cascade hydropower stations and generate more than 300 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity annually, more than three times the annual generation of China’s Three Gorges Dam, according to reports cited in the material.With an estimated cost of around 1.2 trillion yuan, or about $167.8 billion, it is set to rank among the world’s most expensive infrastructure projects. Chinese Premier Li Qiang has described it as the “project of the century”.But the significance of the project extends far beyond its size or power-generation capacity.The Brahmaputra is far more than a river. It is an economic, ecological and strategic lifeline for millions of people across the eastern Himalayas and South Asia.Originating on the Tibetan Plateau, the river flows through China, India and Bangladesh before emptying into the Bay of Bengal. It stretches for roughly 2,900 kilometres and drains a basin of about 580,000 square kilometres shared by China, India, Bhutan and Bangladesh.One of the world’s largest rivers by discharge, the Brahmaputra is also known for its vast braided channels. Its waters support agriculture, irrigation, fisheries, transport, hydropower and ecosystems across the region.For India, the river becomes particularly important after entering Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. The Brahmaputra and its tributaries sustain communities, farmland and ecosystems across the Northeast, while also bringing the region some of its most destructive floods.That is what makes China’s position upstream so significant for India. Beijing cannot simply stop the Brahmaputra from flowing into India. By the time the river reaches Arunachal Pradesh, it has already begun receiving substantial water from rainfall and tributaries, with flows rising sharply during the monsoon.The concern is therefore less about China being able to permanently cut off the river and more about whether a large upstream hydropower system could influence the timing and volume of flows.The operation of reservoirs, tunnels, power stations and other infrastructure could potentially affect seasonal water releases.For India, this raises questions not only about water security, but also about access to reliable hydrological information and the ability to prepare for sudden changes in river flows, particularly during periods of heavy rainfall or extreme weather.What did experts findThe study, published in the Chinese-language journal Sedimentary Geology and Tethyan Geology and supervised by the state-owned China Geological Survey, examined the Paizhen Fault in Tibet.According to the researchers, the fault has remained highly active since the Pleistocene epoch, or Ice Age, and continues to show evidence of geological activity. Geological dating of ancient lake sediments suggests that movement along the fault occurred as recently as about 9,500 years ago.The researchers warned that repeated movement along the fault had fractured and weakened surrounding rock formations. This could make major engineering structures in the area more vulnerable to geological hazards."The Paizhen area is located within the reservoir area of the Yarlung Tsangpo downstream hydropower station," the paper said.The researchers said the fault could have a significant impact on the structural stability and construction of nearby infrastructure, including dams, roads, bridges and tunnels, as well as the reservoir area.They also cited the magnitude 6.9 earthquake that struck the Milin area of Tibet in 2017 as evidence that the region remains seismically active."Under regional seismic action, landslides and collapses can easily be induced, threatening the safety of engineering facilities and personnel," they said.The scientists recommended reinforcing vulnerable slopes and installing retaining structures to reduce the risk of landslides and collapses during construction and after the project becomes operational.The research was conducted by scientists from the Chengdu University of Technology, the Civil-Military Integration Centre of the China Geological Survey, and the Middle Yarlung Zangbo River Natural Resources Observation and Research Station.The findings are significant because they come from Chinese researchers working within China's own geological and scientific institutions.They do not establish that the project is unsafe or that a disaster will occur. But they underline the difficulty of constructing and operating a mega-project in a region where geological instability is an inherent feature of the landscape.Is China capable of ‘stopping’ the Brahmaputra?The idea that China could simply stop the Brahmaputra from reaching India is often overstated. Srijan Pal Singh, author, former Advisor for Policy and Technology to former President APJ Abdul Kalam, CEO of Homi Lab and founder of Kalam Centre, said the more realistic concern was China's ability to influence the timing of flows and the lack of transparency surrounding the management of the river."The real concern, therefore, is less about China cutting off the Brahmaputra and more about transparency, reliable data-sharing, and India's ability to anticipate and manage sudden changes in flow," Singh had earlier told TOI.He said that while a significant share of the Brahmaputra's annual flow is generated within India through monsoon rainfall and tributaries, the lean-season flow originating in Tibet remains strategically important.Singh also cautioned against viewing the project solely through the lens of water diversion. "Any large dam on an international river has both economic and strategic implications," he said.He added that control over upstream infrastructure could itself create strategic influence even without physically restricting the river."It is not necessary to stop the flow of water for leverage to exist. The ability to regulate flows, collect hydrological data, or alter the timing of water releases can shape the decisions of downstream countries, particularly during periods of tension or extreme weather," he said.The distinction matters because the principal challenge for India is not simply the quantity of water but the predictability of that water.During the monsoon, India needs accurate information about upstream river conditions to prepare for floods. During the dry season, information about river flows becomes equally important for agriculture, water management and ecosystems.What India is concernedIndia’s concerns over the Medog project go beyond water security. The Yarlung Tsangpo flows from Tibet into Arunachal Pradesh. A mega infrastructure project on the river, close to the disputed border, therefore has an inevitable strategic dimension.The biggest concern may ultimately be geological. The project lies in the eastern Himalayas, along the collision zone of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates.The region is marked by active faults, steep slopes, fractured rock, earthquakes and frequent landslides, all of which pose challenges for a mega-dam and the infrastructure needed to support it.The 1950 Assam-Tibet earthquake, estimated at magnitude 8.7, remains a stark reminder of the region’s seismic potential. It caused widespread destruction across Tibet and Assam and killed thousands of people.The Chinese geological study has added to concerns over the site. Researchers found that repeated fault activity had weakened rock formations and recommended measures such as reinforcing vulnerable slopes and constructing retaining structures to reduce landslide risks.Writing in Project Syndicate, Brahma Chellaney, professor emeritus of strategic studies at the New Delhi-based Centre for Policy Research, said the warning from Chinese scientists was particularly significant.“The geologists conclude that the terrain has a 'loose structure and weak cohesion' and warn that fault movement or an earthquake could easily trigger large-scale instability, threatening both the reservoir and surrounding infrastructure,” Chellaney wrote.“Ironically, the latest evidence suggests that China's scientific establishment understands the dangers of building the unprecedented super-dam more clearly than its political leadership appears willing to acknowledge. Now that China’s own geologists have raised the alarm, Beijing must embrace transparency and accept transboundary responsibilities before a potential water bomb is fully assembled upstream,” Chellaney wrote on X.There are also concerns about the possibility of reservoir-triggered seismicity, in which the weight of water stored behind a large dam can affect pressure and stress along existing faults. China’s 2008 Wenchuan earthquake has often been cited in this debate.Scientists have differed over the extent of the Zipingpu reservoir’s role, but some studies have suggested that the reservoir may have contributed to triggering or advancing seismic activity.The concern, therefore, is not only whether an earthquake could damage the dam. A major earthquake could also trigger landslides, rockfalls and failures across the surrounding infrastructure.Singh said advances in engineering have significantly improved dam safety but cannot completely remove geological risks.“Modern engineering can design dams to withstand very strong earthquakes. Advanced materials, flexible structural designs and continuous monitoring systems have greatly improved dam safety. However, no engineer can completely eliminate geological risk,” he said.The region has also witnessed glacier collapses and landslides. Sayanangshu Modak, a researcher at the University of Arizona, cited the massive 2021 glacier collapse near the Great Bend, which temporarily blocked the river and sharply raised water levels, SCMP reported.Long-term safety, he added, would depend on continuous monitoring, regular assessments and the ability of the project to withstand not only earthquakes but also landslides, rockfalls and extreme weather events.What does Nepal’s recent disaster show?The August 26 disaster in Nepal offers a stark example of how Himalayan hazards can interact. The evidence available so far points to a glacier-rock collapse and massive debris avalanche rather than a conventional monsoon flood.The collapse triggered an ice-rock avalanche that temporarily blocked the Bhotekoshi River, sending a huge volume of ice, rock, mud and water downstream and causing widespread destruction.The avalanche reportedly travelled at around 50 metres per second. Such events demonstrate the cascading nature of Himalayan disasters.A glacier collapse or earthquake can trigger a landslide; a landslide can block a river; and the sudden failure of that blockage can send a destructive surge of water and debris downstream.Infrastructure located along the river corridor, including roads, bridges, hydropower stations and settlements, can then become part of the disaster chain.The 2015 Nepal earthquake provided another warning. Research following the quake found that earthquake-triggered landslides were a major cause of damage to hydropower infrastructure and estimated that about a quarter of existing, constructed and planned Himalayan hydropower projects faced a high probability of moderate-to-severe earthquake damage.How climate change is adding to the riskClimate change is adding another layer of uncertainty to an already fragile landscape. Glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya are losing ice, while permafrost degradation can destabilise high-altitude slopes. Glacial lakes are expanding in some areas, while changing rainfall patterns are increasing the risk of extreme precipitation.Nepal has thousands of glacial lakes, some of which can potentially produce catastrophic Glacial Lake Outburst Floods, or GLOFs.Climate change does not cause every landslide, avalanche or flood. But it can alter the conditions that make such events more likely and make their timing and scale harder to predict.That creates a particular challenge for hydropower development in the Himalayas.As Himanshu Thakkar, coordinator of the South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People, has argued, environmental, social and disaster-risk assessments need to account for the specific characteristics and historical hazards of individual valleys.The ecological concernsThe Medog project is being built in an exceptionally sensitive landscape. The Great Bend of the Yarlung Tsangpo is marked by steep slopes, glaciers, high rainfall, unstable rock formations and active tectonic structures.Geologist Fan Xiao has described the Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon as a rare biodiversity hotspot in a geologically unstable region.He has warned that multiple hydropower stations, high dams, reservoirs and extensive tunnels could increase landslide risks and cause long-term environmental damage.The impact of such a project is also unlikely to be limited to the dam itself. Roads, tunnels, bridges, transmission lines, worker settlements and other supporting infrastructure will be needed to build and operate the project.Each intervention can alter slopes, drainage patterns and river corridors, creating additional pressure on an already fragile ecosystem.The ecological consequences are particularly difficult to predict over decades, especially as climate change continues to reshape the Himalayan environment.The project’s location also raises questions about its strategic implications for India. The concern is not simply that the dam could alter river flows. The infrastructure required to build and operate such a massive project could itself have strategic value.“Such a large project requires roads, tunnels, bridges, power infrastructure and communication networks. These assets can improve access to remote border areas and support logistics in peacetime as well as during a crisis,” Singh said.He added that while the project alone would not alter the military balance along the Line of Actual Control, it could increase China’s long-term presence near the border and improve its understanding of the terrain and river system.“The strategic balance in the eastern sector will continue to depend primarily on military capability, border infrastructure, surveillance and operational readiness on both sides,” he said.Singh also noted that India has accelerated hydropower development downstream as part of its effort to strengthen water utilisation.Some analysts, however, see the project as giving Beijing additional diplomatic leverage because of its upstream position. Shanghai-based security analyst Ni Lexiong told SCMP that the dam could “effectively create geopolitical leverage vis-a-vis India diplomatically”.Others take a more cautious view. Liu Zongyi, a senior fellow at the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies, argued that concerns about China’s ability to manipulate river flows are overstated and that the project would not fundamentally change India-China relations.For India, therefore, the challenge is broader than the question of whether China can control the Brahmaputra.It is about managing the combined risks of upstream infrastructure, uncertain hydrological flows, seismic hazards, climate change and the project’s proximity to a sensitive border.Dam can affect Earth’s rotationEarth’s rotation is not perfectly constant. Natural forces such as earthquakes, the Moon’s gravitational pull, melting ice and the movement of water can subtly change how quickly the planet spins. Even human-made structures can have a measurable, though extremely tiny, effect.China’s Three Gorges Dam provides one striking example. When its vast reservoir is filled, the enormous volume of stored water redistributes mass on Earth. This increases the planet’s moment of inertia, causing it to rotate very slightly more slowly.Nasa scientist Dr Benjamin Fong Chao calculated that the full reservoir could lengthen the day by about 0.06 microseconds, or 60 billionths of a second, while shifting the position of the poles by roughly two centimetres, BBC reported.The change is far too small to have any noticeable effect on everyday life. But it demonstrates how moving billions of tonnes of water can produce a measurable change in the planet’s physical dynamics.China calls Brahmaputra project safeBeijing has repeatedly sought to reassure downstream countries about the safety of the Medog project. An official statement issued in December 2024 said the project was safe and prioritised ecological protection."Through extensive geological explorations and technical advancements, a solid foundation has been laid for the science-based, secure, and high-quality development of the project," it said.Chinese officials have also maintained that the project follows the highest industry standards and would not negatively affect downstream countries.A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said China was highly responsible in developing cross-border rivers and had extensive experience in hydropower construction. Beijing has also said it would maintain communication with downstream countries and cooperate on disaster prevention and mitigation.The recent geological study does not necessarily contradict those assurances in the sense of proving that the dam is unsafe. But it does demonstrate that the geological challenges identified by outside observers are also being studied by Chinese scientists themselves.The problem of hydrological dataFor India, one of the most important lessons from the past is the importance of reliable river-flow information. China suspended the sharing of hydrological information on the Brahmaputra and Sutlej during the 2017 flood season.In a written reply in the Rajya Sabha on February 8, 2018, the Ministry of External Affairs said China had not provided hydrological information on the Brahmaputra and Sutlej despite existing bilateral agreements. Beijing attributed the interruption to "technical reasons".The suspension occurred during the 73-day Doklam standoff between India and China, although Beijing maintained that the interruption was related to the upgrading of hydrological monitoring stations.China resumed Brahmaputra hydrological data sharing in May 2018. The original agreement on sharing hydrological information for the Brahmaputra was signed in 2002 and subsequently renewed.Why is transparency important?For India and Bangladesh, the challenge is therefore broader than whether China can control the Brahmaputra. It involves the combined risks of upstream infrastructure, seismic hazards, climate change, ecological damage and uncertainty over future water flows.The sheer scale of what China has called the “project of the century” has also increased calls for greater transparency about the dam’s design, geological assessments, reservoir operations and possible downstream impacts.International principles governing transboundary rivers generally require countries to exchange relevant information, avoid significant cross-border harm and consult on projects that could affect other states.Chellaney has argued that China’s limited disclosure about the project is particularly concerning given its potential consequences for downstream countries.Singh said India’s immediate priority should be stronger mechanisms for information-sharing.“India's first priority should be to strengthen institutional mechanisms for the regular exchange of hydrological data, especially during the monsoon season,” he said.Chellaney argued that the warnings raised by Chinese researchers should prompt greater international scrutiny.“When scientists working under a communist regime issue such warnings, the international community must pay attention,” he wrote.For India, the Medog project is therefore not just a question of water. It is a question of how to manage a combination of geological, environmental and strategic risks on a river that crosses national borders and supports millions of people downstream.A Himalayan warning for IndiaThe recent disaster in Nepal has shown how quickly the Himalayas can turn from a source of water and energy into a source of extraordinary danger.A glacier can collapse. Rock can fall into a river. A temporary blockage can form. The blockage can breach. A wall of water and debris can then travel through a narrow valley at enormous speed.When roads, bridges, tunnels, hydropower plants and settlements occupy that same valley, the consequences multiply. This is the central challenge facing Himalayan development.The issue is not whether Nepal, India or China should develop their mountain regions. Millions of people depend on infrastructure, electricity, connectivity and economic development.The question is whether that development is being planned according to the realities of a young, unstable and rapidly warming mountain system.For India, the question becomes even more consequential because the country's major rivers originate or flow through these mountains before reaching the plains.China's Yarlung Tsangpo project therefore represents more than a massive power-generation scheme. It raises questions about seismic safety, river-flow management, ecological change, data sharing and strategic influence.The Himalayas are already under pressure from climate change, earthquakes, landslides, glacier retreat and intense rainfall. Adding more infrastructure without accounting for cumulative risk could create new vulnerabilities even while addressing existing strategic concerns.The immediate cause of Nepal's August 26 disaster may have been a glacier-rock collapse. But the larger warning is unmistakable: the Himalayas are becoming an increasingly dangerous place to ignore geological and climatic limits.As Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah said in his September 2 address to the House of Representatives, "climate change is the world's shared responsibility, and that Nepal must forcefully campaign for climate justice and international financial compensation rather than simple post-disaster aid".He linked the recent catastrophic flash floods in Rasuwa to a warming climate and described the disaster as a warning for the wider Himalayan region and the world.That warning extends beyond Nepal.The Brahmaputra does not recognise borders. Neither do earthquakes, glaciers, landslides or extreme weather. As China moves ahead with the Medog mega-project and India expands its own hydropower infrastructure, the real test will be whether development can keep pace with the risks of a rapidly changing Himalayas.As construction of the Medog project advances, the questions will become increasingly difficult to avoid: Can the world's largest hydropower project remain safe in one of the world's most geologically active landscapes? Can downstream countries receive timely and reliable information about changes in river flows?And can infrastructure development in the Himalayas be pursued without turning natural hazards into human-made disasters?For now, there are no easy answers. But the floods in Nepal have made one thing clear. In the Himalayas, the consequences of getting the balance between development and nature wrong can travel far beyond the valley where the decision was made.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A home run for workers? Daman & Diu’s SPARSH 2.0 opens more rental space
articles.summary: News News: Finding affordable rental housing can be a challenge for workers and other economically weaker sections. To expand access to such housing, the Dadra a.
articles.body: Finding affordable rental housing can be a challenge for workers and other economically weaker sections. To expand access to such housing, the Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu administration has introduced the Scheme for Promotion of Affordable Rental Smart Housing (SPARSH 2.0), which offers incentives to housing complex owners and developers for building or redeveloping affordable rental homes.Implemented by the Labour & Employment Department of the UT Administration of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, the scheme relaxes several construction norms and offers benefits such as additional Floor Space Index (FSI), higher ground coverage, commercial-use flexibility and other regulatory relaxations. In return, eligible housing complexes must reserve at least 66% of their dwelling units for Economically Weaker Section (EWS) beneficiaries.Applicable across Daman, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Diu from 2022 to 2027, SPARSH 2.0 also aims to encourage public and private investment in affordable rental housing, improve workers’ health and well-being, boost industrial productivity and reduce their financial burden from treatment costs and wage loss. It also seeks to improve workers’ happiness and quality of life while harmonising the Affordable Rental Housing Complexes (ARHC) Scheme guidelines with the SPARSH Scheme.So, what does SPARSH 2.0 offer, who can apply and what conditions must housing complexes meet?What is SPARSH 2.0?The scheme seeks to encourage the development and redevelopment of affordable rental housing infrastructure for workers, labourers, urban poor and other weaker sections.Under its vertical for incentivising the development or redevelopment of housing complexes and residential spaces for the urban poor, construction norms are relaxed for eligible SPARSH 2.0 housing complexes. Registered complexes become eligible for further scheme incentives and benefits, while the registration process provides for annual monitoring and compliance verification.What benefits does the scheme offer?Eligible housing complexes can avail several construction and regulatory relaxations.Each housing complex under SPARSH 2.0 is entitled to:Additional 50% of the applicable FSIAdditional 20% ground coverageRelaxations in setbacks or abutting road size, as determined by the concerned authority through applicable rules or bye-lawsUse of 20% of permissible ground coverage for commercial or business purposes, except in the Green Zone and notwithstanding other zone, road-width or area provisionsThe concerned authority can also regularise existing housing complexes if they fall within the relaxed guidelines prescribed under the scheme. The concerned Revenue Departments will prioritise applications for NA for construction of such housing complexes.Which housing complexes can apply?The proposed construction must either be registered under the Affordable Rental Housing Complexes (ARHC) Scheme or fulfil the prescribed SPARSH 2.0 conditions, except condition (g), along with having all other valid permissions required under law. The applicant must belong to Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu and must be the owner or authorised representative of the housing complex.The complex must fulfil SPARSH 2.0 infrastructure norms and possess a valid construction permission and/or occupancy certificate. Applicants must also agree to reserve at least 66% of dwelling units for EWS beneficiaries and maintain the housing complex and its waste management systems.How can applicants register?The owner or authorised representative has to first obtain Form A prescribed under the scheme.The applicant must fill in the form and attach all required supporting documents before submitting the completed application to the concerned officer designated by the Secretary, Labour, for the respective district.The nodal officer will verify the application within 30 days. Technical verification may also be carried out through the Associate Town Planner or another competent authority.After successful verification, the nodal officer will issue the Registration Certificate in Form B and execute an agreement with the owner as prescribed under the scheme.FAQs: SPARSH 2.0 explainedWhat is the objective of SPARSH 2.0 and where does it apply?The scheme aims to encourage the development and redevelopment of affordable rental housing complexes for the urban poor by relaxing construction norms and incentivising eligible owners and developers. It applies across Daman, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Diu from 2022 to 2027. Applicants must belong to Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu and be the owner or authorised representative of the housing complex.What additional construction benefits does SPARSH 2.0 offer?Eligible housing complexes are entitled to 20% additional ground coverage. The scheme also allows relaxations in setbacks or abutting road size, as determined by the concerned authority.Can commercial activities be carried out in the housing complex?Yes. Except in the Green Zone, 20% of the permissible ground coverage may be used for commercial or business purposes.How long does the application process take?The nodal officer is required to verify the application within 30 days. Technical verification may also be undertaken by the Associate Town Planner or another competent authority.What happens after an application is approved?Following successful verification, the nodal officer issues a Registration Certificate in Form B and executes an agreement with the owner as prescribed under the scheme. Registered housing complexes are also subject to annual monitoring and compliance verification.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: 'Second chance': Chimps used in hepatitis B experiments get comprehensive health checks in Liberia
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Chimpanzees once used in hepatitis B vaccine experiments have undergone comprehensive health checks at a sanctuary in Liberia as part of long-term car.
articles.body: Chimpanzees once used in hepatitis B vaccine experiments have undergone comprehensive health checks at a sanctuary in Liberia as part of long-term care aimed at giving the animals a chance to live out their lives in safety.The West African chimpanzees were examined at Humane World for Animals' Second Chance Chimpanzee Refuge in central Liberia, where veterinary teams carried out procedures including dental checks, X-rays, blood tests and nail trimming, sanctuary director Liliana Pacheco Ricote told The Associated Press.More than 400 chimpanzees were used by American researchers in hepatitis B vaccine experiments in Liberia from the 1970s until the early 2000s, Ricote said. Many had been captured from the wild as infants and subjected to invasive procedures during the research.Humane World for Animals said it assumed permanent responsibility in 2015 for the 60 chimpanzees that remained after the research programme ended. The animals now live mainly on a group of mangrove-covered islands at the sanctuary.The latest examinations were conducted under anaesthesia and were designed to provide a head-to-toe assessment of the chimpanzees' health, identify early signs of disease and help veterinarians develop individual care plans as the animals age, the organisation said.The checks included examinations of the teeth, heart, lungs and nervous system, along with blood tests. The chimpanzees also received booster vaccinations and nail trims, with plans to examine the remaining animals."The health checks are a vital part of caring for these chimpanzees who have been through so much," said Belen Perez Hernando, the sanctuary's veterinarian.The chimpanzees are now typically between 30 and 35 years old. The full findings from the latest assessments are still being compiled, so the long-term effects of their time in research remain unclear.Ricote said the physical and behavioural effects of the experiments were nevertheless still apparent in some of the animals."They were used in very invasive research ... (and) went through a lot of experiments and pain," she said.Liberia has the second-largest population of chimpanzees in West Africa after Guinea. West African chimpanzees are classified as critically endangered as their numbers continue to decline.For the sanctuary, the health programme is part of an effort to provide the former research animals with specialised care for the rest of their lives."Seeing how much they hurt about what we've done, it gives me a lot of pleasure ... to give them this second chance to live with dignity the life that they deserve," Ricote said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
