articles.title: The Surprising Reason Koalas Roam More in September
articles.summary: For most of the year, koalas barely move, sleeping tucked into eucalyptus trees day after day. But when September arrives, something shifts in Australia's fo...
articles.body:
Koalas become more active and roam farther during September due to the start of their breeding season.

Young male koalas also travel more during this time to establish their own territories, increasing their risk of danger from predators and vehicles.

During the breeding season, male koalas produce loud bellows to attract females and signal their presence to rival males, creating a noisy environment in koala habitats.

If you decided to go into Australia's forests to watch koalas, you'd likely be surprised that the show wouldn't be too riveting. For most of the year, koalas don't do very much. They spend long stretches of time tucked into the forks of eucalyptus trees resting, sleeping, and occasionally feeding on leaves. However, when September comes around, something changes, and suddenly koalas roam more than they do the rest of the year. Why? Their breeding season is underway.

During the breeding season, koalas are much more active, and they're much louder than usual. It's not just about adult males looking for mates either. This is also a time when young male koalas search for a home of their own. Let's take a deeper look at koala behavior in September.

Koalas are generally solitary animals . They don't form large social groups or spend their days traveling together. Instead, individuals occupy home ranges that can overlap with those of other koalas, creating opportunities for animals to encounter potential mates. However, when Spring in Australia comes around, they become much more active. Male koalas roam more during this time and may travel considerably farther than they ever would the rest of the year. Some can cover substantial distances during the breeding season as they search for receptive females and interact with competing males.

Female koalas also travel more during this time, with the same intention of finding a mate. During this strange period of time, koalas that normally seem almost stationary suddenly appear to be everywhere. A koala that would typically be found high in a tree may suddenly be on the ground. Another might be spotted in a backyard or moving along the roadside. It's quite a unique time for the small animals.

You'll find that many koalas roam more during September, and not just the adults looking for mates. This is also when young koalas reach the point where they need to separate from their mother and find an area for themselves, and it can be a difficult journey. In addition to facing potential predators, young koalas may try to make a home where an adult male has already established their territory. As a result, the young male will be driven away.

You may spot koalas in the most unexpected places during this time because some youngsters are forced to search far and wide. They could find themselves in places that they wouldn't traditionally explore. Wildlife organizations note that young koalas dispersing to establish their own territories can travel considerable distances and face an elevated risk of being struck by vehicles or attacked by dogs. In other words, the same behavior that is essential for koala populations to reproduce and maintain healthy territories can also expose individual animals to danger.

Perhaps the strangest part of the spring transformation is the noise. Koalas have a reputation for being quiet, sleepy creatures. Then the breeding season arrives, and people who live near a koala habitat may suddenly hear a sound that seems completely out of the ordinary.

During mating season, male koalas produce deep bellows , grunts, growls, and snarling sounds. The calls can be surprisingly powerful and may travel great distances. Though the animal making it may be adorable, the sound is anything but cute. In fact, a male koala's bellow has been compared to everything from a snore followed by a roar to the noises made by a pig or hippopotamus.

Why does the koala make these sounds? It all comes down to communication. A male's bellow advertises his presence to other koalas. It can help attract females while also signaling to rival males that another male is occupying the area.

The sound may even encode information about the caller. Research summarized by New South Wales' Environment and Heritage department has found that variation in koala bellows is likely associated with male body size . In this way, the sound could potentially help other koalas assess the animal producing the call. In practical terms, the bellow is a koala's way of announcing, "I'm here." Needless to say, because multiple males may be doing the same thing, the Australian bush can sound considerably noisy during breeding season.

Females can produce a range of sounds, including bellows and high-pitched calls. Typically, when the female produces a low-pitched bellow, it indicates that she's ready to mate. A squawk or a wail may occur during the mating process. Koalas also have different vocalizations associated with interactions or distress. Females and younger koalas may squeak or squawk when threatened or interacting with other animals.

Though it's a fascinating behavior, the fact that koalas roam more during mating season means that they may also be at higher risk of injury or death. Two primary threats increase this time of year:

Vehicle strikes are one of the most serious dangers koalas face, and breeding season can make the problem worse. A koala crossing the road may have little understanding of the danger created by traffic, so it may move slowly or hesitate in the middle of the road. The increased seasonal movement has prompted wildlife authorities to introduce specific measures in areas where koalas and vehicles frequently cross paths.

In 2026, for example, New South Wales installed vehicle-activated koala-zone signs in parts of Sydney's Sutherland Shire. The signs were designed for roads that went through important koala habitats and operated during the August-to-February breeding season, when koalas become more mobile. They may have saved many lives.

There's also an increased chance of dog attacks during September's mating season. A koala that remains high in a tree is generally out of reach of a household dog. But once the koala climbs down and travels on the ground, the situation changes dramatically. Koalas are not built to outrun or fight off dogs, so a confrontation is likely to lead to serious injury. This type of incident is also more common when koalas roam into backyards where dogs may be present.

For people living in or near koala habitat, keeping dogs securely contained after dark can make a meaningful difference. Wildlife officials also recommend that people in these areas use koala-friendly fencing that provides koalas with a way to escape if they enter a yard.

A Busy Season for One of Australia's Most Vulnerable Animals

Spring's increase in koala activity is ultimately a positive sign of a functioning natural cycle. Breeding season gives adults opportunities to find mates, while young animals begin dispersing and establishing territories that can support future generations.

But when koalas roam more, they're also exposed to some of the most dangerous features of the modern Australian landscape. So, if you find yourself in this area during September or the spring season, keep an eye out for a wandering koala. You'll be contributing to the continuation of a happy koala population.

articles.title: Deprogrammed: Ex-OnlyFans manager finds Jesus and goes on a mission to save young women
articles.summary: Former OnlyFans manager Victoria Sinis says sexual liberation is "actually the thing that's crushing us" and shares how Christian faith set her free.
articles.body: Once trapped under the temptation of wealth from the digital exploitation of young women’s bodies, Victoria Sinis is now free from a sordid life as an OnlyFans manager after reclaiming her faith in Jesus. "Coming from someone that believed the lie that sexual liberation and sexual empowerment was to sleep with people, to show off your body as much as possible, to make money off doing that, and now coming into Christian faith… I see things with a totally new set of values," Sinis told Fox News Digital. "We paint [sexual liberation] as freedom, but it’s actually the thing that’s crushing us… [It is] actually the thing that's destroying you. It's the thing that's crushing you. It's a thing that makes you more insecure. It’s the thing that makes you feel worse," she continued. PLAYBOY'S CELEBRITY-DRIVEN RELAUNCH FACES CREDIBILITY TEST IN ONLYFANS ERA, EXPERT SAYS Sinis, whose work as a manager for an OnlyFans agency in Australia began during the pandemic in an effort to improve her finances while reducing the amount of hours she was working in hospitality, now highlights her experience online, exposing the dark underbelly of the adult industry while saving girls from falling prey to the platform. "Once you open up the door for sexuality to be able to have any desire that you want fulfilled, people have to understand it's a never-ending pit. It just keeps going. And so the reason why faith has such strong values around sexuality is because it understands the dangers of when you open that door — it's very hard to close it," Sinis said. "When you understand in a faith lens of, ‘Wow, there's a reason for this, and it's made in a specific and particular way to be able to best express this thing,’ it's the most freedom you can ever have," she said. "I saw firsthand how things like OnlyFans are really destroying men…. There is an entire multi-billion dollar industry that is targeting men, to be able to harness their weakest essence to get them addicted to these platforms, to make money off of them. And in return, it is heightening their loneliness, their depressions, their anxiety, their disconnectedness, their struggles with being able to build healthy relationships," she continued. 'HARRY POTTER' ACTOR SAYS ONLYFANS VIDEOS EARNED HER MORE THAN HER ENTIRE ACTING CAREER "These platforms are really destructive for men, and we need to understand that the more we encourage this, the more that we're actually hurting men as much as we are hurting women," she relayed. Sinus was catapulted over time into searching for a good deed to redeem herself and outdo the bad she felt she was doing. That journey led her back to the church she visited as a child, where she encountered a sermon that "instantaneously clicked" with her spirit, reconnected her with Jesus and helped her leave the industry for good. Sinis, who now travels the world speaking about her experience in the adult industry, points to social media as a main culprit in glamorizing lifestyles that make children and young people idolize career choices like OnlyFans. "Parents are so unaware of what is truly influencing their child. If they have a phone, if they have a laptop, if their friend has a phone, if their friend has an iPad, and they have unlimited Internet access to any type of social media platform, they're going to be influenced by those things unless values are instilled within them that help them to understand that what they're seeing online is not real," she revealed. FORMER DISNEY STAR DAVID HENRIE REJECTED 'SECULAR' HOLLYWOOD LIFESTYLE AFTER LIFE-CHANGING MONASTERY VISIT "I had two 15-year-olds at a private Catholic school in a fantastic area in Melbourne, Australia, tell me that they loved watching this OnlyFans influencer, because she seemed happy and can travel. And so sometimes it's the most innocent of things, but they're now equating to OnlyFans with being happy and travel[ing] — so now they believe that the only way to be happy and to travel is through OnlyFans," Sinis added. "This is the sex industry. It is the same consequences, the same mental health ramifications and the same struggles as any other woman in the sex history. And we need to treat it that way and understand that the struggles that the girls have in OnlyFans really is the same as anyone in escorting prostitution, brothels.. and that way we're able to act in accordance with that and be able to truly help these women to leave [the industry]," Sinis said. An OnlyFans spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "OnlyFans was designed to empower creators to control and monetize their content, and individual creators determine what content they choose to create and how they engage with their audience. Since the platform was established in 2016, more than $30 billion has been paid out to creators around the world, including more than $6 billion in 2025." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

articles.title: Eight-time Grammy winner Art Garfunkel says Trump presidency has him considering leaving US: 'I don't like America's position at all'
articles.summary: US News: Art Garfunkel, the eight-time Grammy-winning singer, says he is considering leaving the United States because of his opposition to President Donald Tr.
articles.body: Art Garfunkel, the eight-time Grammy-winning singer, says he is considering leaving the United States because of his opposition to President Donald Trump’s administration.“I don’t like America’s position at all,” Garfunkel said in an interview with The Guardian. “I’m not aboard, and I’m thinking of leaving the country, frankly.”The 84-year-old musician said Trump’s policies and actions had left him alarmed, while also expressing concern about climate change, rising water levels and global hunger.Garfunkel questioned the administration’s approach to Venezuela, asking whether taking control of another country had become acceptable under “the new rules.”“When Donald Trump took over Venezuela, are those the new rules? Just take over a country and run it? It’s shocking,” he said.Garfunkel has supported Trump’s political opponents, including Bernie Sanders, and has long identified with liberal politics.Although he criticised the current administration, Garfunkel said he believed Trump’s presidency would eventually end.“You think: how on Earth are we gonna change the presidency?” he said. “But Trump won’t last forever. So we’ve got to hope.”Garfunkel has received eight Grammy Awards, including a Recording Academy Lifetime Achievement Award. He is also known for his long musical partnership with Paul Simon. The two singers reconciled in 2025 after years of estrangement.Garfunkel is returning to live performance with his What a Wonderful World tour, which begins in Los Angeles on October 1 before travelling to the UK, France, Germany and Japan. He has said he is singing more now than he has in two decades.His recent work includes Father and Son, an album made with his son Art Jr, and “Authorship”, a track featuring an excerpt from his 2017 memoir over an AI-generated piano arrangement. The song was created for a compilation produced in collaboration with the technology company ElevenLabs.His career began in childhood. Garfunkel met Simon at school in Queens, New York, and the pair recorded together before finding early success as Tom & Jerry. Their 1957 song “Hey, Schoolgirl” became a hit, but the duo later separated as Garfunkel continued his education.The pair reunited professionally as Simon & Garfunkel, scoring major hits including “The Sound of Silence”, “Mrs Robinson” and “Bridge Over Troubled Water”. Garfunkel later pursued a solo career, acted in films including Catch-22 and Carnal Knowledge, and released the 1979 hit “Bright Eyes”.Simon & Garfunkel have reunited for performances over the years, including a 1981 concert in New York’s Central Park attended by hundreds of thousands of people. articles.title: Three hurricanes are still churning in the Pacific, and a fourth may be on the way
articles.summary: Three hurricanes are still active in the Pacific — Karina, Lowell and Marie — and a fourth system could form. Hawaii could see watches for Lowell later Satur...
articles.body:
Three hurricanes are still churning in the Pacific Ocean at the same time — Karina, Lowell and Marie — three days after they made this the first triple-hurricane stretch in a decade. A fourth system offshore southwestern Mexico could soon join them.

It's the first time since 2015 that three simultaneous hurricanes of any strength formed, when Kilo, Ignacio and Jimena all became major Category 4 hurricanes.

This year's El Niño conditions have contributed to hurricane formation in the Pacific and are predicted to soon become the strongest on record.

El Niño affects hurricane severity in both the Atlantic and the Pacific, leading to fewer hurricanes in the Atlantic (particularly the Caribbean) and more in the Pacific due to increased rising air over the tropical Pacific and sinking air over the tropical Atlantic.

Weather changes fast. Get real-time alerts for your area on the new Yahoo Weather app .

Here's the location, path and status of each of the hurricanes:

Hurricane Karina has weakened to a Category 1 storm and is expected to dissipate by early next week without threatening land.

Karina was located about 800 miles east of Hilo, Hawaii.

It had maximum sustained winds of 75 mph.

"Karina is forecast to quickly weaken through early next week," the NHC said.

There are currently no hazards affecting land.

Hurricane Lowell is a powerful Category 4 storm expected to remain a major hurricane through the weekend. NHC forecasters said tropical storm watches will likely be required for parts of the western main Hawaiian Islands and the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument later Saturday. The storm's forecast track has it moving over portions of the monument Monday night.

Lowell was located about 630 miles southwest of Lihue, Hawaii.

It had maximum sustained winds of 150 mph.

"Some fluctuations in intensity are expected during the next few days," according to the NHC. "However, Lowell is expected to remain a major hurricane for the next several days."

Swells generated by Lowell are spreading north and are expected to affect parts of the Hawaiian Islands over the next several days. They're likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip-current conditions.

Hurricane Marie is a Category 1 storm and is expected to weaken during the next few days.

Marie was located about 675 miles west of the southern tip of Baja California.

It had maximum sustained winds of 90 mph.

"Marie is expected to weaken during the next few days," the NHC said.

The NHC is monitoring a fourth area for potential development well offshore of southwestern Mexico. Forecasters give it a 60% chance of developing into a tropical depression by later this week as it moves west-northwest at 10-15 mph. If it forms and gets named, the next name on the East Pacific list is Norbert.

articles.title: Texas opens season against Texas State as Arch Manning faces a make-or-break college football year
articles.summary: Arch Manning enters a make-or-break season as Texas hosts Texas State in a lopsided Week 1 college football matchup with the under 59.5 play.
articles.body: We officially have the first full weekend of college football. From now until the end of the year, we get to watch football essentially all day Saturday and Sunday. Sure, there will be some breaks in there, and some days that won’t have quite as much on the gridiron. Still, I’m pumped to have it back and have more options for sports betting. I mentioned this in another article, but this is not a great week of games, as most are lopsided games. We will likely have one here between Texas State and Texas, but there is still reason for intrigue. STEVE SARKISIAN GIVES EMBARRASSING EXPLANATION FOR TEXAS' COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF LOSS: 'WE WERE TIRED' Money is a major factor in college sports, but with college football being the king of them, there is money galore. I have to imagine that one of the reasons that Texas State agreed to this game is that the school was paid a lot of money to come play Texas. Texas State went 7-6 last year, so it wasn’t like they were awful. However, the best team they played last year was probably Arizona State. They played Rice in a bowl game, so perhaps that was their toughest game. Brad Jackson is back under center for Texas State, so you have to imagine the team will at least know the offense well enough to run coherent plays. Last season he was pretty good. articles.title: Built in 1897, Santa Monica's last intact shotgun house was nearly demolished in 1997; after multiple moves and restoration, it now serves as a preservation centre
articles.summary: US News: A small wooden house in Santa Monica has survived something few historic buildings ever face: demolition threats, years in storage and several moves f.
articles.body: A small wooden house in Santa Monica has survived something few historic buildings ever face: demolition threats, years in storage and several moves from one location to another. Built in 1897, the Shotgun House is now recognised as the last intact example of its kind in the city. What began as a modest home near the beach has become an important piece of Santa Monica's architectural history. Its survival is also a story of residents and preservation groups stepping in when an old building was at risk of disappearing. Today, the house stands at 2520 Second Street, where it has been given a new purpose as a Preservation Resource Center. The Santa Monica Conservancy, which has cared for the property, is marking 10 years since the restored building opened as a community resource in 2016.From beach cottage to landmarkAccording to the Santa Monica Conservancy, the Shotgun House was built in 1897 at 2712 Second Street in Ocean Park, when the neighbourhood was rapidly developing as a seaside resort. Shotgun houses were practical, inexpensive structures that were particularly suited to communities where small vacation cottages were needed near the beach. The house was originally only a short distance from the Santa Fe railroad depot and local tourist attractions.The architectural form itself has a longer history. Architectural historians believe the shotgun house originated in the Caribbean through a blend of African and European influences before becoming widespread in the American South during the 19th century. Its simple design made it inexpensive to construct and relatively easy to move, while its narrow footprint allowed it to fit on small lots. Santa Monica's example consists of three small rooms arranged in a row. It has a board-and-batten exterior, a covered front porch and a gabled roof. Although the design is relatively plain, diamond-shaped shingles on the front gable add a touch of Queen Anne styling.Nearly lost to demolitionThe house survived as a residence for almost a century, remaining occupied until 1996. By that point, however, many of Santa Monica's other shotgun houses had already disappeared. Some had been demolished after being considered unsafe, while others were lost as development transformed the city. The Shotgun House itself came close to the same fate. The Santa Monica Conservancy says community members and preservation advocates helped save the structure from demolition beginning in the late 1990s, with the preservation effort continuing through 2002. The effort involved concerned residents, the former Ocean Park Community Organisation, the Church at Ocean Park, the Conservancy and the City of Santa Monica. The building was designated a landmark in 1999. But saving it did not mean the house immediately had a permanent home.A house that kept movingThe structure went through a complicated relocation process. After becoming the property of the City, it was moved multiple times over the following years. The Conservancy's history records that the house was relocated three times before reaching its permanent location in 2014. Its final journey took the historic structure to Second Street, across from the Ocean Park Library. At the time, the move was significant enough for members of the public to watch as the small house was transported on a flatbed trailer through Santa Monica streets. The move finally provided an opportunity to give the building a purpose beyond simply preserving it.From home to resource centreUnder the Santa Monica Conservancy's guardianship, an adaptive-reuse plan was developed to rehabilitate the house while retaining its historic character. Funds were raised to restore the structure and transform it into a Preservation Resource Center. The centre officially opened in January 2016. Rather than functioning as a private residence, the restored building now helps people understand Santa Monica's historic places and the principles of preservation. It provides information for residents, property owners, students, visitors and others interested in local history. It also offers tours and educational programming. The building itself is also an example of adaptive reuse. The Conservancy describes it as a model showing how a historic structure can be rehabilitated and given a useful role in modern community life. The project earned a LEED Gold rating, while the surrounding Shotgun House Coastal Garden uses drought-resistant native plants.Ten years of preservationIn 2026, the Shotgun House marks a decade as the Preservation Resource Center. The house's story is ultimately about more than one 19th-century building. Its survival shows how preservation can work when an old structure is not treated simply as an obstacle to development. A building that once served as a modest vacation-era home, nearly disappeared in the late 20th century and spent years being moved around Santa Monica now has a permanent role in teaching the city's history. At 129 years old, the little Shotgun House has therefore gained something its original builders could hardly have anticipated: a second life as a place dedicated to making sure historic places are not forgotten.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court lawyer Amita Sachdeva has filed a complaint at the cyber police station in New Delhi against a minor protester linked to the Jantar Mantar protest and her father Sanjay Azad. The complainant alleged that posts from the minor’s X account contained derogatory references to Bhagwan Shiv, Bhagwan Shri Krishna, Maa Saraswati and Maa Durga.“I am a practising Hindu. I viewed the posts listed below on X (formerly Twitter) while at the Supreme Court of India, New Delhi. The posts remain publicly available and have outraged my religious feelings and those of other Hindus,” news agency ANI reported Sachdeva saying.Sachdeva has sought registration of an FIR under Sections 299 and 196 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), besides applicable provisions of the Information Technology Act, 2000.According to the complaint, four posts uploaded between September 2023 and August 2026 allegedly insulted Hindu deities and religious beliefs. Sachdeva alleged the posts were published with deliberate and malicious intent to “outrage the religious feelings” of Hindus. She said she had earlier sought their removal but they remained online.The lawyer has sought preservation of the posts, associated media and platform records, including IP logs, device details and other electronic evidence. She has also sought steps to prevent further circulation of the alleged content.The complaint is separate from an alleged assault case involving the minor’s father during a CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in July. CJP has accused self-styled influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj of assaulting him, while Bhardwaj has claimed the incident was an act of self-defence.Bhardwaj was detained by Delhi Police on Friday from Bulandshahr and was remanded to one day of police custody after being produced before a court in Delhi on Saturday.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘We’ve got to be careful’: Ex-CDS Anil Chauhan flags Pakistan's 'overconfidence' after Mecca Pact
articles.summary: News News: Former chief of defence staff Gen Anil Chauhan has cautioned that the recent defence agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye could induce.
articles.body: Former chief of defence staff Gen Anil Chauhan has cautioned that the recent defence agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye could induce “overconfidence” in Islamabad and lead it to make another “miscalculation”.Speaking at an event at the Teen Murti Bhawan complex in New Delhi on Saturday, Chauhan said Pakistan would remain a major security concern for India.“But, we've also seen some kind of agreements and accords with they have recently signed. This sometimes, I feel, may induce some kind of an overconfidence into Pakistan, and they may make some kind of a miscalculation again. We've got to be careful about that,” he said.His remarks came nearly a month after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on August 7. Under the pact, an attack against any one of the three countries will be treated as an attack against all three.Chauhan calls Pakistan a continuing security concernDelivering the 22nd Bharat Ratna Pt Govind Ballabh Pant Memorial Lecture on ‘Threats and Challenges to India's Security’, Chauhan said India’s security environment was shaped by several factors, including unresolved borders, cross-border terrorism, non-state actors and competition in areas such as space, cyber and the maritime domain.“Let me talk about our western neighbour. So Pakistan will remain, I think, a major security concern and a threat for times to come,” he said.He said Operation Sindoor, India’s decision to hold the Indus Water Treaty in abeyance and other practical measures could “hopefully change or induce behavioural change in our neighbour”.Chauhan was serving as CDS when Operation Sindoor was conducted in May last year. The operation followed the April 22 Pahalgam attack.Even after retiring in May 2026, Chauhan has said Operation Sindoor is “not over” but on pause, and has called for continued operational readiness by the armed forces.Terrorism, proxy war and nuclear deterrenceChauhan described terrorism and proxy war as central to Pakistan’s approach towards India, arguing that nuclear weapons had reduced the scope for conventional operations while creating space for sub-conventional activities.“The existing of nuclear weapons has created a degree of static stability at the apex level. And this is what has induced instability at the lowest level. So it's classically known as a stability-instability paradox,” he said.He said Pakistan’s strategy had been to reduce the scope for conventional operations while expanding “sub-conventional operations”, including terrorism and cross-border activities.According to Chauhan, non-state actors can provide deniability and lower the apparent cost of such operations, while terrorist networks can be rebuilt through ideology, recruitment, financing, training, propaganda and state support.He said terrorism and proxy war would remain a “major challenge” for India and argued that the response should involve credible deterrence.“And the only way you can defeat is to create credible deterrence. And that's what we demonstrated in three cross-border operations -- Uri, then Balakot, and then Operation Sindoor,” he said.He added that India needed to raise the cost of proxy war and terrorism for Pakistan so that Islamabad stopped using them “as an instrument of state policy”.Future warfare will require faster adaptationChauhan also spoke about how technology was changing the nature of warfare and the requirements for India’s armed forces.“The future will favour the forces that learn, adapt faster than their adversaries,” he said, adding that the military would need capabilities across traditional and emerging domains, including land, sea, airspace, cyber, the electromagnetic spectrum and cognitive and synthetic domains.He stressed the importance of jointness and integration among the armed forces.“Jointness and integration are essential because technology erases organisational boundaries faster than bureaucracies do. Sensors, decision-makers, and shooters must be connected across all domains,” Chauhan said.He attributed part of India’s performance during Operation Sindoor to what he described as better battlefield transparency and situational awareness, which enabled faster decision-making.He said services and domains supported by a common operational picture and a resilient network would be important for future military operations.

articles.title: Detransitioner takes malpractice fight to appeals court after North Carolina law change
articles.summary: Prisha Mosley's detransition lawsuit against doctors who advised her double mastectomy and hormone therapy heads to a North Carolina appeals court.
articles.body: A detransitioner’s malpractice lawsuit against doctors she says counseled her for years to undergo a double mastectomy and begin hormone therapy was initially dismissed as untimely, but a new North Carolina law has allowed her to appeal. The state Court of Appeals will hear arguments on Sept. 29. Prisha Mosley, now 28, was first prescribed hormones at 17 and underwent a double mastectomy at 18. She later sued the doctors and other medical providers for fraud and malpractice, alleging they misled her about the treatment and its effects. "I'm a mammal, a human, so I wasn't able to change sex. I didn't need to change sex because that's not possible and nothing was ever wrong with my body. Destroying it with hormones and surgery did not make me happy or well," she told Fox News Digital in an interview. A trial court in North Carolina initially dismissed Mosley's lawsuit on the basis of the statute of limitations. But, as Mosley explained to Fox News Digital, a law passed in North Carolina in 2025 extended the statute of limitations for medical malpractice lawsuits specifically for people who have undergone gender transitions. DETRANSITIONER WINS SETTLEMENT AFTER SUING PROVIDERS FOLLOWING GENDER SURGERY "During the process through which my lawsuit was going through the courts, North Carolina passed HB 808, which was previously HB 805, which is something along the lines of the Protect Children and Women's Act," Mosley explained. "[The law] extended the statute of limitations for anyone bringing forward a civil case, and even had a line which said that this includes cases that have already been brought forward or even pending in the courts now," she continued. Legislators in North Carolina passed the bill in 2025, overriding a veto from Democratic Gov. Josh Stein. INSURANCE COMPANIES PUT ON NOTICE FOR STRANDING TRANS PATIENTS WHO WANT TO REVERSE SURGERIES FTC ALLEGES INFLUENTIAL TRANSGENDER HEALTH ORGANIZATION MISLED PARENTS ABOUT SAFETY OF YOUTH TREATMENTS Though the bill was passed in July 2025, a North Carolina trial judge still dismissed Mosley's lawsuit in August 2025, denying her lawyers' motion to reinstate her medical malpractice claims during a special session and granting summary judgment to the plaintiffs. "Despite this, my claims were dismissed with prejudice, even though they had been previously found to have merit for fraud. The malpractice was still in question due to the statute of limitations, and then after the passage of the law, the entire case was dismissed," Mosley told Fox News Digital. TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROBE COULD UPEND WIDELY USED TRANSGENDER YOUTH TREATMENT GUIDELINES Mosley was initially encouraged by the judge's decision to deny the defendants' motion to dismiss, taking it as a signal her fraud accusations could have merit. "The judge actually originally found that my case did have merit for fraud, and that was on the basis that I was told that I could actually change sex, which is not possible, and I was not only told that I could change sex, but that I needed to do so in order to survive and that doing so would ensure I had a good life. All of these claims are false," she told Fox News Digital. WOMAN WHO LIVED AS MAN SAYS SHE GRIEVED ‘UNWANTED BODY PARTS’ AFTER TRANSITION But after her lawsuit's final dismissal in August, her lawyers appealed, leading to the upcoming Sept. 29 appellate court oral arguments. Mosley is arguing that the doctors who counseled her into the double mastectomy and hormone therapy misled her by telling her she could become a man and go through male puberty, which she says was a lie. AT 14, I ENDURED ‘GENDER-AFFIRMING CARE.’ I’LL SUFFER WITH THAT FOR THE REST OF MY LIFE "I consented to quote unquote top surgery, and I was under the impression that top surgery was the surgery that turned a female chest into a male chest, and that's simply not what happened to me. In fact, I had complications related to my surgery," she told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Clearly I didn't have a male chest, and the guarantees weren't promised that way. But it's also impossible to induce puberty of the opposite sex because it's impossible to change sex. I wasn't going through male puberty. I was being put through menopause as a teenager, and while inducing all of these medical issues and problems for me, my doctors just covered it up with these fraudulent terms that made it seem like something good and medically sound was happening to me when it was not. Even when I complained about side effects and said that I was suffering from pain and acne and other issues, they told me that this was because of male puberty," she explained. Mosley said that she realized she had been lied to when, though she was still identifying as a male at the time, her fiancé's young daughter kept referring to her as "mommy." "Despite the fact that I still had a beard at the time and I was wearing male clothes and all of that, this little girl started calling me mommy, and that's just where everything fell into place for me," she told Fox News Digital. Mosley said she was encouraged by a recent ruling in New York, where 22-year-old detransitioner, Fox Varians, sued the psychologist and plastic surgeon who counseled her to undergo a gender transition, winning $2 million in a judgment. Mosley pointed out that no detransitioners suing their medical providers for malpractice have ever lost their cases in trial. "I think it's clear to people that this type of medicalization is wrong, and it points to the fact, you know, Fox Varian's is the only detransitioner case that's ever made it to court. None of our cases, not mine, not anyone else's, have ever failed in court. We're being stopped by strange policies and statutes of limitations before we ever go before a jury. But the general public knows that what happened to us is wrong and that we deserve justice for what happened to us," she told Fox News Digital. Fox News Digital contacted Stein's office and legal representatives for each of the defendants listed in Mosley vs. Emerson for further comment.

articles.title: Meet Harvey Uyeyama, the 16-year-old from Davis, California who learned coffee roasting from his father and built a subscription business after his death
articles.summary: US News: At 16, Harvey Uyeyama already has a business, a loyal customer base and a highly specialized craft that most adults never attempt to master. From his .
articles.body: At 16, Harvey Uyeyama already has a business, a loyal customer base and a highly specialized craft that most adults never attempt to master. From his home in Davis, California, the soon-to-be high school senior hand-roasts coffee, customizes orders and runs a growing subscription service, all while preparing for college. But Harvey’s Coffee began with something much more personal, the time spent with his father. According to a report by The Sacramento Bee, Uyeyama learned to roast coffee from his father, John, who had previously owned a coffee shop in Lafayette and continued roasting at home. In June 2024, his father invited him to join him for a late-night roasting session. The two spent hours working together, beginning what would become the foundation of Harvey’s Coffee. Entrepreneurship was already familiar territory for Uyeyama. As a child, he tried everything from running a lemonade stand to tutoring math in an effort to make money. Coffee, however, was different. His father had given him a skill he could turn into something of his own. He began selling freshly roasted beans door-to-door around his neighborhood. The first customers did not come easily. After plenty of rejection, Uyeyama refined his sales pitch and presentation, eventually swapping a black backpack for a wagon and adding branded labels to make the business look more professional.Finding purpose through griefNot long after teaching his son the craft, John Uyeyama died on his son's birthday. The loss brought roasting to a temporary halt. But just a few weeks later, coffee unexpectedly brought Harvey back to the craft. His father’s funeral service needed coffee, and Harvey took on the job despite having never completed an entire roasting process alone. The experience was difficult, involving plenty of mistakes and ruined batches. But the coffee was well received by mourners, giving Harvey a renewed sense that roasting could be more than a business. It could also be a way of carrying forward something his father had passed down to him.Building a business with patienceToday, Uyeyama operates Harvey’s Coffee with his girlfriend, Abby Merchant, an 18-year-old student at UC San Diego. While Merchant is studying biology, she has taken on an important role in the company’s branding and marketing, redesigning its logo, packaging and overall customer experience. Uyeyama focuses on roasting and the technical side of the operation. He has even built an app to manage sales and recurring subscriptions. The company is approaching 100 monthly subscribers, with customers spread across the country. Each month, Uyeyama chooses beans from a different region, examining factors such as acidity, body, flavor and the history behind each coffee. Although he particularly enjoys East African coffees, he deliberately changes the selections to keep the subscription experience interesting.An old-school approach to modern coffeeHarvey’s Coffee is anything but mass-produced. Uyeyama roasts every batch by hand on a machine believed to date back to the early 1900s. The antique-looking roaster uses rotating chambers positioned above propane burners. Uyeyama manually adjusts the heat throughout the process, watching temperatures, listening for the beans to crack and inspecting their color as they develop. The machine can handle about four bags at a time, allowing him to produce roughly 12 bags an hour. Each order is then packaged by hand, with codes and customer names identifying where the coffee is headed. Local customers can receive their coffee within 24 hours of roasting, while shipments travel to subscribers across the United States.Looking aheadUyeyama plans to graduate early after one final semester, giving him roughly nine months to expand the company before heading to college. Scaling up could mean a warehouse, larger equipment, a new grinder and a more sophisticated setup. But one thing is unlikely to change: the human touch. For Uyeyama, the future of Harvey’s Coffee is not about automation. It is about keeping every batch deliberate, personal and handcrafted — much like the first batch he made alongside his father on a late night in June 2024.Images Courtesy: istock and The Sacramento BeeCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: United Nations votes 164-1 for Equal Earth map after US brands it 'radical ideological project'
articles.summary: The United Nations adopted the Equal Earth map showing Africa's true size, but the United States was the sole nation to vote against the resolution.
articles.body: The United Nations on Friday was one vote shy of unanimously adopting a new map of the world that shows Africa's true size, making the continent appear far larger than it does on traditional maps. The United States was the only one of the 165 member nations to vote against the UN General Assembly resolution to accept the Equal Earth map projection, which depicts countries and continents in their true relative sizes, according to the map creator's website. Six nations abstained, including Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia and Ukraine. Yaryna Ferencevych, the deputy U.S. representative to the U.N. Economic and Social Council, said the resolution was presented as "an anodyne effort to update cartographic proportions" but was, in her view, part of a "much larger and more radical ideological project." TRUMP ADMINISTRATION REJECTS UN MIGRATION DECLARATION, SAYS 'MASS MIGRATION WAS NEVER SAFE' "Instead of focusing on genuine problems of international peace, prosperity, or good relations, this body is debating map projects from the 16th century and their role in promoting reparations and cognitive justice," Ferencevych said Friday during the 114th Plenary meeting. "Resolutions like this one and the ideological agenda they promote are barnacles on our work here and the reason this institution is losing its credibility," she added. Ferencevych was referring to the Mercator projection, created in 1569 to aid maritime navigation. To this day, it is seen as the traditional world map and is used in many school textbooks and atlases. It enlarges land masses near the poles and reduces the apparent size of those near the equator, making Africa appear far smaller relative to Greenland and Europe than it is in reality. AFRICAN AND CARIBBEAN LEADERS CALL FOR PAYMENTS, DEBT CANCELLATION, FORMAL APOLOGIES OVER SLAVERY Togo Foreign Minister Robert Dussey, who introduced the resolution on behalf of the African Group, said that adopting the new map would "promote projections that better preserve the true proportions of continents." "A fair map does not change the geography of the world; it changes how we see the world," he said. "And when our perspective becomes more just, it paves the way for greater understanding, respect and peace among nations." The measure does not require countries or companies to abandon the Mercator projection, but it establishes the U.N.'s official backing for equal-area maps as the preferred way to depict the world. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Mercator projection largely fell out of favor among cartographers in the 20th century because of its distortions. However, it saw a resurgence after Google Maps adopted the Web Mercator projection in 2005, with virtually every major online mapping service following suit. Web Mercator became the standard for online maps because it allowed for smooth panning and zooming across the globe, making it well suited for interactive digital maps, according to a 2014 Cartographica study. The United States Mission to the United Nations and the ECOSOC did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

articles.title: Influencers reaching peak backlash after summer of ruined destinations and experiences for Americans
articles.summary: A growing backlash against influencers and content creators is occurring this summer at a variety of locations, including OpenAI's luxury retreat, World Cup matches and Nantucket getaways.
articles.body: Everyday Americans are growing increasingly annoyed by social media influencer stunts and takeovers at famous landmarks, major events and vacation destinations once prized for the enjoyment, relaxation and serenity they usually bring — all for the sake of a few self-promoting photos, videos and "likes." From locations as varied as sports stadiums and luxury resorts, influencers are now facing bans, arrests and rejection this summer. Numerous onlookers have had enough, as Fox News Digital and other outlets have been reporting. SOCIAL MEDIA PHOTO CRAZE SPARKS TOURIST INVASION AT PICTURE-PERFECT VACATION HOT SPOT Here are just a few of the hot spots where social media influencers have been wearing out their welcome — and ruining experiences for everyday Americans as well as local business owners. 1. Hudson Valley, New York OpenAI, an artificial-intelligence technology company, hosted a group of content creators in August for a "Summer Camp" trip at Wildflower Farms, a luxury retreat in Upstate New York's Hudson Valley. The retreat sparked controversy, with many blasting the nature-focused getaway given concerns about the environmental toll of data centers needed to power AI. ONCE-GLAMOROUS VACATION SPOT OVERRUN BY INFLUENCERS AND CROWDS: 'ALMOST UNBEARABLE' "Sending them to nature before they turn it into a data center," one X user wrote. An OpenAI spokesperson defended the trip, telling The Hollywood Reporter that creators are an important part of the company's community and that they play a part in how people learn about products — adding that OpenAI welcomes healthy debate. 2. The World Cup Argentinian YouTube content creators Lautaro "Beni" Mármol, 20, and Patricio "Pato" Perrotta, 26, were arrested at this year's World Cup. They were charged with interference at a sporting event after authorities said they bypassed three layers of security. The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office wrote in arrest reports that Mármol said he was a media influencer trying to get in to stream the game, and that Perrotta said he was "hired by a media company to review the event and has credentials, but they were from a previous event," as WPLG Local 10 reported. 3. Nantucket, Massachusetts An island about 30 miles off the coast of Cape Cod, Massachusetts, Nantucket is accessible only by airplane or ferry. That remote access has long made it an exclusive and much-loved summer destination for many. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS But content creators have been infuriating a number of locals. Four Winds Craft Guild, a third-generation business approaching its 100th year, recently hung a sign saying, "No Influencers," as Fox News Digital previously reported. Store owner John Sylvia told The New York Times that it sometimes appears his store is a stage. "I don't have this hatred toward influencers," he clarified. "It was more of a joke. It is a problem we should look at as a society." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Sylvia's partner, Jessica Jenkins, told the outlet she felt deluged by "people creating videos on corners of themselves sipping an iced coffee and looking over their shoulder and doing a shoe kick or whatever." Fox News Digital previously reached out to Four Winds Craft Guild for comment. 4. Baja California Sur, Mexico In early August, Aman Hotels was at the center of a dispute with a YouTuber who attempted to stay at the luxury hospitality group's new Amanvari resort on the East Cape of Baja California Sur, Mexico. Hotel reviewer Ryan Walker posted a video to YouTube alleging he paid $4,663 for a one-night stay at Amanvari — claiming the hotel canceled his reservation and called the police when he arrived. Aman took issue with Walker's account. As The Wall Street Journal reported, Amanvari emailed Walker five days before his stay and asked him to postpone because the resort was under a month-long media blackout. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The resort told him he was welcome — but that he could not film in public areas and would need permission to do so in private spaces, the outlet said. 5. He posted a viral video that appeared to show him trying to eat chicken nuggets while riding a famous roller coaster at Cedar Point in Sandusky, Ohio, which is owned by Six Flags, as Fox News Digital previously reported. articles.title: Russia’s Putin meets US envoys to discuss Trump proposal to end Ukraine war
articles.summary: Both Russia and Ukraine vow not to strike each other’s capitals for three days during talks in Moscow and Kyiv.
articles.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has begun talks with United States envoys on ending more than four years of war in Ukraine, ahead of their first visit to Kyiv expected on Sunday.

Putin met Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner – respectively President Donald Trump’s special envoy and business ally, and his son-in-law – at the Kremlin on Saturday.

“Dear colleagues, I warmly welcome you to Moscow. The situation is, of course, not simple,” Putin told the envoys in a grand Kremlin hall in footage aired by Russian TV.

Both Russia and Ukraine vowed not to strike each other’s capitals for three days during the negotiations, as Washington tries to revive US-led talks to end Europe’s worst conflict since World War II.

Trump earlier said Kushner and Witkoff were bringing “a proposal to end the war”.

In Putin’s address to the two men, he said: “I would like to ask everyone to convey their best wishes and words of gratitude to US President Mr Trump”.

Witkoff said Trump had sent his best wishes to Putin and ⁠thanked him for ⁠the limited ceasefire during the delegation’s visit. Putin said ⁠Russia would do its ⁠utmost to ensure ⁠the safety of the mediators.

The talks come as the grinding war – which began with a Russian invasion in 2022 – has seen increasing civilian deaths and attacks this summer.

Putin has repeatedly said Moscow intends to seize the rest of east Ukraine.

Russian strikes on Ukraine on Saturday killed at least seven people, including in the Kyiv suburbs, Ukrainian officials said.

The Kremlin said it would not strike Kyiv from midnight on Saturday, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he would halt strikes on Moscow “from now” until Monday.

“The Russian president, the commander-in-chief, has given the order from midnight tonight not to strike Kyiv for three days,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.

Zelensky – who had offered a truce during the US visits – later said he had spoken to the US envoys and also promised Kyiv would not strike Moscow.

“From now through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday, Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow,” Zelensky said on social media.

The Ukrainian leader said he had spoken to the US officials and that he expected them in Kyiv on Sunday.

It will be the first time that Witkoff and Kushner visit Kyiv since Trump returned to office last year with a pledge to resolve the conflict.
